norms.text: If an appellate court shall determine that an appeal is frivolous it may award damages to the respondent as the court shall deem just and proper.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 559 sanctionne l’appel principal dilatoire ou abusif par une amende civile pouvant être assortie de dommages-intérêts. La Rule 84.19 permet d’accorder des dommages-intérêts en cas d’appel frivole, tandis que le RSMo 512.160(4) prévoit des dommages-intérêts après confirmation ou rejet, sans amende civile spécifique.
correspondences.note_en: Article 559 sanctions a dilatory or abusive principal appeal with a civil fine and potentially damages. Rule 84.19 permits damages for a frivolous appeal, while RSMo 512.160(4) permits damages after affirmance or dismissal, but neither provides the same civil-fine mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 560 permet d’accorder des dommages-intérêts contre celui qui interjette appel après s’être abstenu sans motif légitime de comparaître en première instance. La Rule 84.19 vise les appels frivoles et le RSMo 512.160(4) les dommages-intérêts après confirmation ou rejet, sans reprendre la condition de non-comparution.
correspondences.note_en: Article 560 authorizes damages against an appellant who unjustifiably failed to appear at trial. Rule 84.19 addresses frivolous appeals, and RSMo 512.160(4) allows damages after affirmance or dismissal, but neither incorporates the article’s specific failure-to-appear condition.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 581 sanctionne le recours dilatoire ou abusif par une amende civile pouvant atteindre 10 000 euros, sans préjudice de dommages-intérêts. La Rule 84.19 permet des dommages pour appel frivole, et le RSMo 512.160 autorise certains dommages en cas de confirmation ou de rejet, mais aucun ne reprend exactement l’amende et le régime de l’article 581.
correspondences.note_en: Article 581 authorizes a civil fine of up to €10,000 for a dilatory or abusive remedy, without prejudice to damages. Rule 84.19 permits damages for a frivolous appeal, and RSMo 512.160 allows certain damages after affirmance or dismissal, but neither reproduces the article’s exact fine and framework.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 628 sanctionne le pourvoi abusif par une amende civile et une indemnité au profit du défendeur. La Rule 84.19 permet d’accorder des dommages-intérêts en cas d’appel frivole, tandis que le RSMo 512.160 autorise certains dommages en cas de confirmation ou de rejet, mais aucun des deux ne reprend exactement le régime de l’amende civile.
correspondences.note_en: Article 628 sanctions an abusive cassation appeal with a civil fine and an award to the respondent. Rule 84.19 permits damages for a frivolous appeal, and RSMo 512.160 permits certain damages after affirmance or dismissal, but neither reproduces the civil-fine scheme exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1247 permet, en cas de rejet de l’appel, de condamner l’appelant — sauf le juge — aux dépens et à des dommages-intérêts. Les règles du Missouri prévoient séparément la charge des frais d’appel et l’octroi éventuel de dommages pour appel frivole, affirmation ou rejet, avec des conditions et effets différents.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1247 permits the rejected appellant—except the judge—to be ordered to pay costs and damages. Missouri separately addresses appellate costs and possible damages for frivolous appeals, affirmance, or dismissal, but under materially different conditions and effects.

norms.heading: Procedure as to Original Writs

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Relating to All Appellate Courts
Rule 84 — Procedure in All Appellate Courts

norms.text:
(a) Proceedings on petitions for original remedial writs shall be as prescribed in these Rules 84.22 through 84.26 and in Rules 91 through 98 as applicable. Petitions for original remedial writs shall be accompanied by a docket fee in the amount specified by Rule 81.04(d).
The petition shall be filed by the clerk of the court to which it is presented upon presentation of:

(1) The petition and the writ summary, which shall not exceed one page exclusive of the caption and identity of the parties and their attorneys in the underlying action, substantially in conformity with Civil Procedure Form No. 16;
(2) Suggestions in support of the petition;

(3) The docket fee; a statement citing specific statutory or other authority demonstrating a docket fee is not required by law; or a motion to proceed in forma pauperis; and

(4) Proof of service, prior to or on the day of presentation of the petition for filing, of a copy of the petition, the writ summary, and the suggestions in support of the petition upon the respondent and, if applicable, all parties in the underlying action. Such proof of service shall state the name, address, electronic mail address, and telephone number of:
(A) Each attorney served and the name of the party such attorney represents, and

(B) Each self-represented party served.

(b) The filing of a petition for an original remedial writ does not affect the authority of the respondent to act or the validity of the respondent's action.

(c) Within ten days after the filing of the petition for an original writ, the respondent may file suggestions in opposition to the issuance of the writ. Within that same time, any party in the underlying matter may file suggestions in opposition, either individually or jointly with any other person filing such suggestions.
(d) Except as provided in Rule 84.24(e), the writ shall not issue before the expiration of the time for the respondent to file suggestions in opposition to the issuance of the writ. A denial of the petition for the writ may be made at any time after filing of the petition. If a preliminary writ is issued, an answer to the petition shall be filed within such time as the court specifies by order.
Within that same time, any party in the underlying matter may file an answer to the petition, either individually or jointly with any other person filing an answer. In issuing a preliminary writ, appellate courts may use the forms approved for use in the circuit courts or employ other language as the circumstances may require.
(e) Whenever in the judgment of the court the purpose of the writ would be defeated if the time limits set forth in Rule 84.24(c) or Rule 84.24(d) are enforced, the court, on motion of the petitioner or relator or on its own motion, may shorten the time for filing suggestions in opposition to the petition or dispense with such time limits altogether, and it may issue the writ upon the expiration of the time as so shortened or, if the court dispenses with such time, immediately.
(f) Oral argument will not be granted on petitions for original remedial writs.

(g) The petition for the writ, together with the suggestions in support thereof, any exhibits accompanying the petition, all suggestions in opposition, the writ and return of service thereon, the answer made to the petition for the writ, and all other papers, documents, orders, and records filed in the appellate court constitute the record. No record under Rule 81.12 is required.
(h) If the writ is issued, briefs shall be filed as is required on appeals, except that the time for filing the briefs shall be as follows: The brief of the petitioner or relator shall be filed within 30 days from the answer date in the preliminary order; respondent's brief shall be filed within 20 days thereafter; and if petitioner or relator desires to file a reply brief, it shall be filed within ten days thereafter. When a master is appointed, the time for filing briefs shall date from the filing of the report or, if exceptions are filed, from the time of disposition of the exceptions.
(i) Whenever in the judgment of the court the procedure heretofore required would defeat the purpose of the writ, the court may dispense with such portions of the procedure as is necessary in the interest of justice.
(j) No petition for a writ of habeas corpus for the purpose of having the petitioner admitted to bail in any criminal case, either before trial or while such is pending in the appellate court upon appeal, shall be considered unless service of the petition and suggestions in support thereof, as required by Rule 84.24(a), be made upon the attorney general in cases pending upon appeal or otherwise on the prosecuting officer of the jurisdiction in which such criminal case originated.
(k) If a permanent writ in mandamus or prohibition is ordered to issue, the court shall issue an opinion setting out its reasons for issuing the writ. The opinion shall be filed contemporaneously with the order to issue the writ or, if exigent circumstances require, within a reasonable time after the issuance of the writ.
(l) If a permanent writ is denied without an opinion issuing, a motion for reconsideration of the court's action, however denominated, shall not be filed.

(m) If the court disposes of a petition for a writ by the issuance of an opinion, further review of the action shall be allowed only as provided in Rule 83 and Rule 84.17.

correspondences.note_en: Article 846 governs how a petition is presented, including who may submit it and filing with the clerk. Rule 43.02 regulates filing with the clerk, while Rules 84.24 and 90.02 provide comparable filing mechanisms for particular petitions or applications.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1030 impose la signification au défendeur, dans les quinze jours, de l’ordonnance autorisant la demande en faux, avec sommation de déclarer s’il entend utiliser la pièce et transmission de la requête et de l’ordonnance. correspondences.note_en: Article 1030 requires service on the defendant within fifteen days of the authorization order, with a demand to state whether the allegedly forged document will be used and copies of the petition and order. Rule 84.24 concerns proof of service for writ petitions; Rule 84.026 concerns initial appellate filings; and Rule 43.01 sets general service methods, without this demand or deadline.

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
(a) Electronic Filing. Except as otherwise specifically provided, this Court and the court of appeals require most documents to be electronically filed. Rule 103 and Court Operating Rule 27 govern the electronic filing of documents and apply if there is a conflict with any other Rule. When filing a document in an appellate court, Rule 103 and Court Operating Rule 27 should be reviewed as well as the local rules of the court in which the document is to be filed. If a document is filed electronically, no paper copies are required to be filed except as provided by local court rule.

(b) Paper Filing. Those who are ineligible to file documents electronically shall comply with all provisions of Rules 81 to 84 except the documents shall be filed in paper form with the clerk's office and shall comply with Rule 81.21 as to format.

(c) Notice. Any notice from the court shall be made to the registered users through the electronic filing system and to all others as provided in Rule 43.01.

correspondences.note_fr: Le greffe informe sans délai les parties et le ministère public de la décision sur la transmission d’une QPC, précise les voies de recours et les modalités d’observations devant la Cour de cassation, et adresse une lettre recommandée aux parties non comparantes. Les textes du Missouri prévoient certaines notifications par le greffe ou la juridiction dans le cadre des appels et de la procédure d’appel, mais ne mentionnent pas la QPC ni ses effets spécifiques.
correspondences.note_en: The clerk must promptly notify the parties and the public prosecutor of the decision on transmitting a constitutional question, state the appeal and observation procedures, and send registered mail to nonappearing parties. The Missouri provisions provide for certain clerk or court notices in appeals and appellate procedure, but do not mention constitutional questions or their specific effects.

correspondences.note_fr: Le greffe notifie aux parties la décision du président ou de son délégué et la date de l’audience. La Rule 84.025 prévoit les notifications de la cour aux utilisateurs du système électronique et aux autres personnes selon la Rule 43.01, qui régit aussi la notification des ordres et avis, sans viser spécifiquement cette décision ni cette audience.
correspondences.note_en: The clerk must notify the parties of the presiding judge’s decision and the hearing date. Rule 84.025 addresses court notices through the electronic filing system or under Rule 43.01, which also governs service of orders and notices, but neither specifically targets this decision or hearing date.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 729-1 autorise la tenue numérique du répertoire, du dossier et du registre, impose l’intégrité, la confidentialité et la conservation, et prévoit la certification de conformité des pièces numérisées. Les règles du Missouri organisent surtout le dépôt électronique et le dossier d’appel numérique, sans reprendre toutes ces garanties ni la restitution des originaux papier.
correspondences.note_en: Article 729-1 permits digital maintenance of court indexes, files, and registers, requiring integrity, confidentiality, preservation, and certification of scanned copies. The Missouri provisions mainly regulate electronic filing and electronic appellate files; they do not reproduce all those safeguards or the return of paper originals.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise la transmission électronique des actes, pièces, avis, convocations, rapports, procès-verbaux et décisions, sous réserve des modalités du titre ou de règles spéciales. Les règles du Missouri organisent surtout le dépôt électronique et la signification électronique, sans couvrir l’ensemble de ces actes ni selon un régime unique.
correspondences.note_en: The article authorizes electronic transmission of procedural documents, exhibits, notices, summonses, reports, records, and enforceable copies, subject to the Title’s modalities or special rules. The Missouri provisions mainly regulate electronic filing and electronic service, without covering all listed documents under a single regime.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article autorise, avec consentement préalable, l’envoi électronique par le greffe d’avis, convocations et récépissés via un portail, avec garanties d’identification, d’intégrité, de confidentialité, de conservation et de datation. La Rule 43.01 permet la signification par courriel et en fixe l’accomplissement, tandis que la Rule 84.025 organise les notifications électroniques aux utilisateurs enregistrés, sans reprendre toutes ces conditions.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits clerks, with prior consent, to send notices, summonses, and receipts electronically through a portal subject to identification, integrity, confidentiality, preservation, and dating safeguards. Rule 43.01 allows service by email and defines when it is complete, while Rule 84.025 provides electronic appellate notices, but neither reproduces all of these conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet, avec consentement révocable, l’envoi confidentiel par courriel de certains avis du greffe et fixe des règles particulières de date et de qualification de la notification selon la réception. La Rule 43.01 reconnaît la signification par courriel et la rend accomplie lors de la transmission, mais ne prévoit pas ces conditions de consentement, de confidentialité ou d’effets de réception.
correspondences.note_en: The article permits confidential email delivery of specified clerk notices with revocable consent and establishes special rules for the effective date and characterization of service. Rule 43.01 recognizes service by email and makes it complete upon transmission, but does not provide the same consent, confidentiality, or receipt-based effects.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose la remise électronique des actes devant la cour d’appel, prévoit une exception en cas d’impossibilité étrangère et organise le dépôt papier, la date de dépôt et les avis électroniques. Les règles du Missouri imposent largement le dépôt électronique et prévoient le dépôt papier et la notification électronique, mais sans reprendre toutes ces modalités ni la sanction française.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires electronic filing in the court of appeal, provides a paper-filing exception for an external impediment, and regulates filing dates and electronic notices. Missouri rules broadly require electronic filing and provide for paper filing and electronic notice, but do not reproduce all these procedures or the French sanction.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article exclut le défenseur syndical de l’obligation électronique et organise pour lui le dépôt papier, les exemplaires et le récépissé postal. Les règles du Missouri traitent les parties inéligibles au dépôt électronique et leurs modalités de dépôt et de notification, sans viser une catégorie identique ni reprendre les règles particulières d’exemplaires et de récépissé.
correspondences.note_en: The article exempts the union representative from electronic filing and regulates paper filing, copies, and postal receipts. Missouri rules address parties ineligible for electronic filing and their filing and service procedures, but do not identify the same category or reproduce the specific copy and receipt requirements.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise l’avis d’audience donné par le greffier lorsqu’une requête saisit la cour, avec transmission de la requête selon que l’avocat est obligatoire ou non. Les Rules 84.025 et 84.026 régissent les notifications et significations dans les cours d’appel, et la Rule 100.02(d) la signification d’une requête de révision, mais aucune ne reprend exactement ce mécanisme.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs clerk-issued hearing notice after a petition invokes the appellate court, including transmission of the petition depending on whether counsel is required. Rules 84.025 and 84.026 address appellate notices and service, and Rule 100.02(d) service of a review petition, but none reproduces the mechanism exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1028 organise le dépôt devant le premier président d’une demande spéciale en faux et exige, lorsque le ministère est obligatoire, la signature d’un avocat aux Conseils. Les règles 84.025 et 84.01 prévoient respectivement le dépôt devant la juridiction d’appel et la signature des actes, sans instituer la demande en faux ni l’exigence d’un avocat spécialisé.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1028 governs filing a special forgery claim before the first president and requires, where representation is mandatory, signature by a specialized appellate lawyer. Rules 84.025 and 84.01 address appellate filing and signatures, but do not create a forgery proceeding or require specialized counsel.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose au greffe d’adresser à la Cour de cassation la décision et les écritures, et prévoit l’information des parties et de certaines autorités. Les Rules 84.025 et 84.026 concernent le dépôt et la notification dans les juridictions d’appel, mais non la transmission du dossier ni l’information des autorités désignées.
correspondences.note_en: This article requires the clerk to send the referral decision and submissions to the Court of Cassation and provides notice to parties and specified officials. Rules 84.025 and 84.026 address appellate-court filing and service or notice, but not transmission of the record or notice to the specified officials.

norms.heading: Service of Filings in Appellate Courts

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

Rule 84 — Procedure in All Appellate Courts

norms.text:
(a) Initial Filings. The electronic filing system does not serve the initial filings on parties. For any new case filed in the electronic filing system in this Court or the court of appeals, including but not limited to initial filings pursuant to Rules 81.07, 83.01, 83.04, 84.035, and 84.24, service of the initially filed documents shall be made pursuant to Rule 43.01 with a certificate of service.

(b) Subsequent Filings. For filings on an existing case, registered users serve and receive service of all filings through the electronic filing system; no additional service or certificate of service is required.

(c) Parties Ineligible to Use the Electronic Filing System. If any party is ineligible to file documents through the electronic filing system, service after the initial filing shall be made as follows:

(1) Each registered user shall serve documents as provided by Rule 43.01 on every ineligible party;

(2) Each ineligible party shall serve documents as provided by Rule 43.01 on every party not represented by an attorney. Service of the documents need not be made on parties represented by an attorney; the notice generated by the electronic filing system shall constitute service on such parties.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe les modalités des notifications et convocations, notamment la lettre recommandée avec accusé de réception et, pour les avocats, le bulletin du greffe. La Rule 43.01 encadre les modes et la date d’accomplissement du service, tandis que la Rule 84.026 règle spécifiquement le service dans les cours d’appel, mais selon des modalités différentes.
correspondences.note_en: The article specifies how notices and summonses are served, including registered mail with acknowledgment and clerk bulletins for attorneys. Rule 43.01 governs methods and completion of service, while Rule 84.026 specifically addresses appellate-court service, but the methods differ.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article exige en principe le consentement exprès du destinataire, prévoit certaines formes de consentement au système électronique et rend ce consentement irrévocable. Les règles du Missouri organisent la signification électronique et le statut des utilisateurs inscrits, mais ne posent pas une exigence générale de consentement exprès et irrévocable.
correspondences.note_en: The article generally requires the recipient’s express consent, recognizes specified forms of consent to electronic communication, and makes consent irrevocable. Missouri rules regulate electronic service and registered users, but do not impose a general requirement of express and irrevocable consent.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit un avis électronique de réception ou de mise à disposition indiquant la date et, le cas échéant, l’heure, qui remplace visa, cachet et signature et dispense de certains exemplaires matériels. Le Missouri reconnaît la notification générée par le système, fixe l’achèvement de la transmission électronique et assimile la signature électronique à l’original, mais sans reprendre exactement ces effets.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires an electronic acknowledgment of receipt or availability stating the date and, where applicable, time; it substitutes for required receipt formalities and eliminates certain paper-copy requirements. Missouri recognizes system-generated notice, defines completion of electronic transmission, and gives electronic signatures the effect of originals, but does not reproduce the same rule in full.

correspondences.note_fr: Les dispositifs électroniques doivent assurer l’identification, l’intégrité, la sécurité, la confidentialité, la conservation et la preuve des dates, et l’identification peut valoir signature. Les Rules 43.01 et 43.02 règlent respectivement le service, le moment de sa réalisation, le dépôt électronique, l’effet du dépôt et la conservation de l’original signé. La Rule 84.026 organise le service électronique dans les juridictions d’appel, sans reprendre toutes les garanties techniques.
correspondences.note_en: Electronic systems must ensure identification, integrity, security, confidentiality, preservation, and proof of dates, and identification may constitute a signature. Rules 43.01 and 43.02 address service timing, electronic filing, filing effects, and retention of the signed filing. Rule 84.026 organizes electronic service in appellate courts without matching all technical safeguards.

correspondences.note_fr: Le greffe notifie la déclaration aux intimés et, en l’absence de constitution, impose une signification dans un délai déterminé avec des avertissements procéduraux. Les Rules 84.026, 43.01 et 81.04 organisent la notification et le service de l’appel, mais ne reproduisent pas ce mécanisme complet ni ses délais et sanctions.
correspondences.note_en: The clerk notifies respondents and, if they do not appear, requires service within a specified period with procedural warnings. Rules 84.026, 43.01, and 81.04 address notification and service of the appeal, but do not reproduce the full mechanism, deadlines, or sanctions.

correspondences.note_fr: Dès sa constitution, l’avocat de l’intimé doit en informer l’avocat de l’appelant et remettre son acte au greffe. La Rule 55.035 régit l’entrée en scène de l’avocat, tandis que les Rules 43.01 et 84.026 organisent le service, sans imposer exactement cette double formalité.
correspondences.note_en: Upon appearing, respondent’s counsel must notify appellant’s counsel and provide the appearance filing to the clerk. Rule 55.035 governs counsel’s entry of appearance, while Rules 43.01 and 84.026 govern service, but none imposes exactly this combined requirement.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 906-1 impose la signification rapide de la déclaration d’appel et des avertissements procéduraux à l’intimé. Les Rules 43.01 et 84.026 régissent la signification des actes et des actes initiaux en appel, mais sans reprendre ces délais ni ces sanctions spécifiques; la Rule 81.04 concerne le dépôt et la notification de l’appel.
correspondences.note_en: Article 906-1 requires prompt service of the notice of appeal and specific warnings to the respondent. Rules 43.01 and 84.026 govern service of papers and initial appellate filings, but do not reproduce these deadlines or sanctions; Rule 81.04 addresses filing and notice of the appeal.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 906-2 fixe les délais de dépôt et de notification des conclusions, assortis de caducité ou d’irrecevabilité, avec possibilité de modification et d’écartement en cas de force majeure. La Rule 84.05 règle les délais des mémoires et leur modification, la Rule 84.08 le défaut de poursuivre l’appel, et la Rule 84.026 la notification électronique des actes ultérieurs.
correspondences.note_en: Article 906-2 sets filing and service deadlines for appellate submissions, with dismissal or inadmissibility sanctions, possible modification, and relief for force majeure. Rule 84.05 governs appellate brief deadlines and their adjustment, Rule 84.08 addresses failure to pursue an appeal, and Rule 84.026 governs electronic service of later filings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose la notification simultanée des conclusions et pièces, le dépôt d’une copie au greffe avec preuve de notification et l’irrecevabilité des pièces soutenant des conclusions irrecevables. Les règles du Missouri organisent la notification, le dépôt et le dépôt des pièces, sans prévoir cette simultanéité ni cette sanction spécifique.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires simultaneous service of briefs and exhibits, filing a copy with proof of service, and inadmissibility of exhibits supporting inadmissible briefs. Missouri rules address service, filing, and appellate exhibits, but not the same simultaneity or sanction.

correspondences.note_fr: Après le dépôt, le greffe français avise l’adversaire, lui adresse la déclaration et annonce une convocation ultérieure. RSMo 512.070 et la Rule 81.04(g) organisent la notification par le greffe de l’acte d’appel aux autres parties, avec des modalités et effets différents; la Rule 84.026 concerne le service des actes initiaux en appel.
correspondences.note_en: After filing, the French clerk notifies the opposing party, sends the notice of appeal, and advises that a later summons will issue. RSMo 512.070 and Rule 81.04(g) require clerk notification of the appeal to other parties, but with different methods and effects; Rule 84.026 addresses service of initial appellate filings.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 946 prévoit une procédure orale, la dispense de comparution, l'organisation des échanges écrits et l'information sur la date du délibéré. Les Rules 84.026 et 43.01 organisent la notification et la preuve de la transmission des écritures, mais ne reprennent pas l'ensemble de ce régime oral.
correspondences.note_en: Article 946 provides for oral proceedings, excused appearance, court-organized written exchanges, and notice of the decision date. Rules 84.026 and 43.01 govern service and proof of appellate filings, but do not reproduce the full oral-procedure framework.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 947 impose l'information des parties non avisées verbalement de la date des audiences ultérieures. Les Rules 84.026 et 43.01 permettent la notification des actes et écrits en appel; la Rule 63.01 concerne la fixation des procès et ses délais de préavis, sans régler spécifiquement les audiences ultérieures en appel.
correspondences.note_en: Article 947 requires parties not notified orally to be informed of later hearing dates. Rules 84.026 and 43.01 facilitate service of appellate filings and notices, while Rule 63.01 addresses trial settings and advance notice rather than later appellate hearings specifically.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise l’avis d’audience donné par le greffier lorsqu’une requête saisit la cour, avec transmission de la requête selon que l’avocat est obligatoire ou non. Les Rules 84.025 et 84.026 régissent les notifications et significations dans les cours d’appel, et la Rule 100.02(d) la signification d’une requête de révision, mais aucune ne reprend exactement ce mécanisme.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs clerk-issued hearing notice after a petition invokes the appellate court, including transmission of the petition depending on whether counsel is required. Rules 84.025 and 84.026 address appellate notices and service, and Rule 100.02(d) service of a review petition, but none reproduces the mechanism exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 977 organise la notification de la déclaration de pourvoi au défendeur, avec notification à l’avocat ou signification subsidiaire. Le § 512.070 prévoit la notification de l’appel par le greffier, mais sans obligation comparable de constituer un avocat ; les Rules 84.026 et 43.01 encadrent le service des actes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 977 governs notice of the appeal declaration to the respondent, including notice to counsel or substitute service. Section 512.070 provides clerk mailing of the notice of appeal, but not a comparable mandatory counsel requirement; Rules 84.026 and 43.01 regulate service.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 978 impose le dépôt et la notification du mémoire dans un délai déterminé, ainsi qu’une présentation structurée et précise des moyens, sous sanctions. La Rule 84.04 encadre le contenu des briefs et des points invoqués ; les Rules 84.05, 84.026 et 84.08 prévoient respectivement les délais, le service et les conséquences des défauts.
correspondences.note_en: Article 978 requires timely filing and service of a structured memorandum, with precise grounds and sanctions for defects. Rule 84.04 governs brief contents and points relied on; Rules 84.05, 84.026, and 84.08 address deadlines, service, and consequences of default.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article régit la signification au défendeur non constitué et les avertissements relatifs à la constitution d’un avocat, au délai de réponse et au pourvoi incident. Les règles du Missouri organisent la signification des actes d’appel au parti ou à son avocat, sans reprendre ces avertissements ni ces effets procéduraux particuliers.
correspondences.note_en: This article governs service on an unrepresented respondent and notices concerning counsel, the response deadline, and a possible cross-appeal. Missouri provisions govern service of appellate filings on the party or attorney, but do not reproduce those warnings or procedural effects.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 990 impose au greffier de notifier sans délai au défendeur une copie du mémoire par lettre recommandée avec demande d’avis de réception. La Rule 84.026 organise la notification des actes dans les affaires d’appel, et la Rule 43.01 les modalités générales de signification, sans imposer exactement cette intervention du greffier ni ce mode unique.
correspondences.note_en: Article 990 requires the clerk to promptly notify the respondent by registered mail with acknowledgment of receipt. Rule 84.026 governs service of appellate filings and Rule 43.01 supplies general service methods, but neither imposes precisely the same clerk duty or exclusive method.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 992 impose au greffier de notifier au demandeur le mémoire en réponse et, en cas de pourvoi incident, au défendeur une copie du mémoire. Les règles 84.026 et 43.01 organisent le service des actes et écritures ultérieurs en appel, mais non cette notification spécifique par le greffe en procédure de cassation.
correspondences.note_en: Article 992 requires the clerk to notify the petitioner of the respondent’s memorandum and, for a cross-appeal, the opposing party of the relevant memorandum. Rules 84.026 and 43.01 govern service of subsequent appellate filings, but not this specific clerk notification in a cassation proceeding.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 1005 impose au demandeur de notifier au défendeur, dans le mois de la déclaration, une copie de son mémoire par lettre recommandée avec avis de réception, sous peine d'irrecevabilité d'office. Les Rules 84.026 et 43.01 organisent le service des actes d'appel, mais sans ce délai ni cette sanction spécifiques.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1005 requires the applicant to serve the respondent with a copy of the memorandum by registered mail with acknowledgment within one month, on pain of dismissal for inadmissibility. Rules 84.026 and 43.01 govern service of appellate filings, but do not impose this specific deadline or sanction.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 1006 fixe au défendeur un délai de quinze jours pour déposer un mémoire en réponse au greffe et en notifier copie au demandeur. La Rule 84.05 prévoit les délais de dépôt des mémoires d'appel, tandis que les Rules 84.026 et 43.01 régissent le dépôt et le service, mais avec des délais et modalités différents.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1006 gives the respondent fifteen days to file a response memorandum with the clerk and serve a copy on the applicant. Rule 84.05 sets appellate brief deadlines, while Rules 84.026 and 43.01 address filing and service, but under materially different deadlines and procedures.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 1007 permet de notifier le mémoire à l'avocat constitué, notamment entre avocats, et assimile la remise contre récépissé portant le cachet daté du greffe à une notification. Les Rules 43.01, 84.026 et 55.035 prévoient le service à l'avocat constitué, sans cette institution ni ces formalités spécifiques.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1007 permits service on counsel who has appeared, including lawyer-to-lawyer service, and treats delivery against receipt bearing the clerk’s date stamp as service. Rules 43.01, 84.026, and 55.035 provide for service on appearing counsel, but not these specific institutional and receipt formalities.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1030 impose la signification au défendeur, dans les quinze jours, de l’ordonnance autorisant la demande en faux, avec sommation de déclarer s’il entend utiliser la pièce et transmission de la requête et de l’ordonnance. La règle 84.24 concerne la preuve de signification des requêtes en writ; la règle 84.026 concerne les dépôts initiaux en appel; la règle 43.01 fixe les modalités générales de signification, sans cette sommation ni ce délai spécifique.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1030 requires service on the defendant within fifteen days of the authorization order, with a demand to state whether the allegedly forged document will be used and copies of the petition and order. Rule 84.24 concerns proof of service for writ petitions; Rule 84.026 concerns initial appellate filings; and Rule 43.01 sets general service methods, without this demand or deadline.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose au greffe d’adresser à la Cour de cassation la décision et les écritures, et prévoit l’information des parties et de certaines autorités. Les Rules 84.025 et 84.026 concernent le dépôt et la notification dans les juridictions d’appel, mais non la transmission du dossier ni l’information des autorités désignées.
correspondences.note_en: This article requires the clerk to send the referral decision and submissions to the Court of Cassation and provides notice to parties and specified officials. Rules 84.025 and 84.026 address appellate-court filing and service or notice, but not transmission of the record or notice to the specified officials.

correspondences.note_fr: La demande est déposée au greffe de la Cour de cassation après signification préalable de certaines décisions aux défendeurs. Les règles du Missouri encadrent le dépôt initial en appel et sa signification, mais n’exigent pas cette signification préalable des décisions.
correspondences.note_en: The application is filed with the Court of Cassation clerk after prior service of specified decisions on the respondents. Missouri rules govern initial appellate filing and service, but do not require this prior service of the decisions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise la notification de la déclaration de réexamen au défendeur, la signification en cas d’échec et l’information sur la constitution d’un avocat et le délai de réponse. Les Rules 84.026 et 43.01 régissent la signification des actes en appel, mais sans reprendre ces modalités propres au réexamen.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs service of the reopening declaration, substituted service if notification fails, and notice of counsel and response deadlines. Rules 84.026 and 43.01 address service of appellate and other filings, but do not reproduce these reopening-specific procedures.

correspondences.note_fr: En l’absence d’avocat constitué, la signification est faite à la partie et l’acte l’informe de l’obligation de constituer un avocat ainsi que du délai de réponse. Les Rules 43.01 et 84.026 distinguent la signification à la partie et à l’avocat; Rule 55.035 traite de la constitution d’avocat, sans imposer exactement ces mentions.
correspondences.note_en: When no attorney has appeared, service is made on the party and the document explains the need to retain counsel and the response deadline. Rules 43.01 and 84.026 distinguish service on parties and attorneys, while Rule 55.035 addresses entry of appearance, without requiring these exact notices.

correspondences.note_fr: Le greffier de renvoi doit transmettre aux parties la déclaration et faire citer les défaillants selon les règles applicables aux défendeurs. La Rule 84.026 organise le service des actes introductifs en appel, tandis que les Rules 43.01 et 54.13 règlent le service et la citation, sans reprendre exactement cette procédure.
correspondences.note_en: The remand clerk must send the declaration to the parties and summon nonappearing parties under the rules applicable to defendants. Rule 84.026 governs service of initial appellate filings, while Rules 43.01 and 54.13 govern service and summons, but do not replicate this procedure exactly.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1037-1 organise la procédure devant la cour de renvoi après cassation : fixation accélérée, signification de la saisine, délais de conclusions, intervention et sanctions de caducité ou d’irrecevabilité. Les Rules 84.05, 84.026, 84.08 et 84.02 traitent respectivement des délais de mémoires, de la notification, du défaut de procédure et de la mise au rôle, mais sans régime spécifique de renvoi après cassation.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1037-1 governs proceedings on remand after cassation, including expedited scheduling, service of the remand filing, briefing deadlines, intervention, and sanctions for default. Rules 84.05, 84.026, 84.08, and 84.02 address briefing deadlines, service, procedural default, and docketing, but do not create a specific post-cassation remand procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: Le greffier convoque les parties, avocats et ministère public à l’audience d’appel, avec notification par lettre recommandée et possibilité d’intervention. Le § 512.070 RSMo prévoit la notification du dépôt de l’appel par le greffier, tandis que les Rules 84.026 et 43.01 organisent la signification des actes; aucune disposition ne reprend entièrement la convocation à l’audience ni le rôle du ministère public.
correspondences.note_en: The clerk summons the parties, attorneys, and prosecuting authority to the appellate hearing, using registered notice and allowing intervention. RSMo 512.070 addresses clerk notification of the appeal, while Rules 84.026 and 43.01 govern service of filings; none fully reproduces the hearing summons or the prosecuting authority’s role.

correspondences.note_fr: La convocation doit être envoyée dès la fixation de l’audience et au moins quinze jours avant, par lettre recommandée, avec copie par lettre simple; elle vaut citation. Le § 512.070 RSMo et les Rules 43.01 et 84.026 prévoient des mécanismes de notification ou de signification, mais sans ce délai ni cet effet de citation.
correspondences.note_en: The summons must be sent when the hearing is scheduled and at least fifteen days beforehand by registered mail, with a simple-mail copy, and it operates as a summons. RSMo 512.070 and Rules 43.01 and 84.026 provide notice or service mechanisms, but not the same deadline or summons effect.

norms.heading: Execution or Remand by Appellate Court – Costs

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rules Relating to All Appellate Courts
Rule 84 — Procedure in All Appellate Courts

norms.text: The court, upon the determination of any cause on appeal, may award execution to carry the same into effect, or may remand the cause with its decision therein, including any judgment or order as to costs made by the appellate court, to the court from which the cause was appealed, and such determination shall be carried into execution by that court.

source_ids.text_source: Perplexity cached copy of the courts.mo.gov page (pplx_sdk.content.fetch)

correspondences.note_fr: Le CPC exonère certaines saisines successives liées au même litige, notamment les recours, renvois après cassation et demandes de modification d’une décision. Les règles du Missouri organisent les appels, le renvoi et le contrôle postérieur du jugement, sans prévoir l’exonération correspondante de frais.
correspondences.note_en: The CPC exempts certain successive proceedings concerning the same dispute, including appeals, remands after cassation, and requests to modify a decision. Missouri rules govern appeals, remand, and post-judgment control, but do not provide the corresponding fee exemption.

correspondences.note_fr: La cour renvoie l'affaire à la juridiction qu'elle estime compétente, et ce renvoi s'impose aux parties et au juge de renvoi. Les règles du Missouri prévoient le renvoi par la juridiction d'appel au tribunal inférieur avec la décision, mais dans le cadre général de l'appel plutôt que pour incompétence.
correspondences.note_en: The French article requires remand to the court deemed competent and makes the decision binding on the parties and the remitting court. Missouri provisions allow an appellate court to remand a case with its decision for execution, but as a general appellate mechanism rather than specifically for jurisdictional incompetence.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 90 permet l’appel global d’un jugement statuant à la fois sur la compétence et le fond, puis impose à la cour soit de statuer au fond, soit de renvoyer l’affaire. Les textes du Missouri prévoient l’appel, les pouvoirs de décision au fond et le renvoi, mais pas ce mécanisme propre à la compétence.
correspondences.note_en: Article 90 permits an appeal of the entire judgment and specifies when the appellate court must decide the merits or remand after reversing on jurisdiction. The Missouri provisions address appealability, appellate disposition, and remand, but do not provide this jurisdiction-specific mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 91 limite l’appel à la compétence lorsque le jugement statuant aussi sur le fond est rendu en dernier ressort, et organise le renvoi après infirmation. Le Missouri reconnaît le contrôle des questions de compétence et règle l’appel, la décision et le renvoi, sans prévoir cette limitation ni l’irrecevabilité correspondante.
correspondences.note_en: Article 91 restricts the appeal to jurisdiction when the merits judgment is rendered as a final-instance decision and provides for remand after reversal. Missouri addresses jurisdictional review, appealability, disposition, and remand, but not this exclusive jurisdictional appeal or the stated inadmissibility rule.

correspondences.note_fr: La cassation rétablit les parties dans leur situation antérieure et annule de plein droit les décisions qui en dépendent ; elle peut aussi mettre certaines parties hors de cause. Le Missouri prévoit la réformation, le règlement définitif, le renvoi et l’exécution de la décision d’appel, sans organiser expressément ces effets consécutifs.
correspondences.note_en: Cassation restores the parties to their pre-judgment position, automatically nullifies dependent decisions, and may remove parties from the remand proceedings. Missouri provides reversal, final disposition, remand, and execution of the appellate decision, but does not expressly provide these consequential effects.

correspondences.note_fr: En cas de cassation avec renvoi, la Cour désigne la juridiction de renvoi, qui statue conformément aux règles applicables. Les textes du Missouri permettent à la juridiction d’appel de renvoyer l’affaire avec sa décision au tribunal d’origine, mais ne prévoient pas ici le mécanisme français de désignation.
correspondences.note_en: After a reversal with remand, the French court designates the remand court, which then decides under the applicable rules. Missouri allows the appellate court to remand the case with its decision to the originating trial court, but does not provide the French designation mechanism here.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 630 confère l’exécution forcée à l’arrêt pour l’amende, l’indemnité et les dépens. La Rule 84.28 permet à la juridiction d’appel d’ordonner l’exécution ou de renvoyer la décision au tribunal inférieur, et la Rule 77.06 prévoit l’exécution pour les dépens, mais le régime n’est pas identique.
correspondences.note_en: Article 630 makes the judgment enforceable for the fine, award, and costs. Rule 84.28 permits an appellate court to award execution or remand its decision for execution, and Rule 77.06 permits execution for costs, but the mechanisms are not identical.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 631 prévoit qu’après cassation, l’instruction reprend devant la juridiction de renvoi dans l’état de la procédure non atteint par la cassation. Le § 512.160(5) et la Rule 84.28 prévoient le renvoi et l’exécution de la décision d’appel, sans reprendre expressément cette règle sur l’état de la procédure.
correspondences.note_en: Article 631 provides that, after cassation, proceedings before the remand court resume in the procedural state unaffected by the cassation. RSMo 512.160(5) and Rule 84.28 provide for remand and enforcement of the appellate disposition, but do not expressly address resuming the unaffected procedural record.

correspondences.note_fr: La juridiction de renvoi statue sur tous les dépens exposés devant les juridictions du fond, y compris ceux liés à la décision cassée. Le Missouri prévoit le renvoi d’une décision relative aux frais et des règles générales de répartition ou de taxation des coûts, sans attribuer expressément cette compétence globale à la juridiction de renvoi.
correspondences.note_en: The remand court determines all costs incurred in the lower courts, including costs connected with the reversed decision. Missouri permits remand of an appellate costs determination and contains general rules on allocation and taxation of costs, but does not expressly confer this comprehensive authority on the remand court.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 729 impose au greffier de transmettre le dossier à la juridiction compétente en cas de recours ou de renvoi après cassation, dans un délai déterminé, et d’en copier les pièces nécessaires. La Rule 84.28 prévoit le renvoi de la cause par la juridiction d’appel, tandis que la Rule 83.01 prévoit, dans un autre contexte, la transmission du dossier lors d’un transfert.
correspondences.note_en: Article 729 requires the clerk to transmit the case file to the proper court after an appeal or remand following cassation, within a specified period, and to copy necessary documents. Rule 84.28 governs appellate remand, while Rule 83.01 concerns forwarding the record on transfer; neither reproduces the full clerk-duty and deadline rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 972 organise la transmission du dossier par le greffe de la cour d’appel à la juridiction de première instance après renvoi ou lorsque l’affaire reprend devant elle, ainsi que le retour du dossier et la jonction d’une copie de la décision. La Rule 84.28 prévoit le renvoi de la cause avec la décision, tandis que la Rule 84.16 concerne la transmission ou remise de la décision, sans régler tout le circuit du dossier.
correspondences.note_en: Article 972 governs transmission of the case file by the appellate clerk to the trial court after remand or resumption, and requires a copy of the appellate decision to accompany it. Rule 84.28 provides for remand of the cause with the decision, while Rule 84.16 addresses transmission or furnishing of the decision but not the full file-routing scheme.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article impose la signature du président, du rapporteur et du greffier, ainsi que la transmission de la décision à la juridiction d'origine. La Rule 41.08 encadre les modalités de signature, tandis que la Rule 84.28 permet le renvoi de la cause avec la décision, sans imposer ces formalités précises.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires signatures by the president, reporting judge, and clerk, and transmission of the decision to the originating court. Rule 41.08 governs signature methods, while Rule 84.28 permits remand with the decision, without imposing these precise formalities.

correspondences.note_fr: Lorsque l’affaire est renvoyée devant une juridiction du fond, les règles du renvoi après cassation s’appliquent. Rule 84.28 et RSMo 512.160(5) permettent le renvoi de la cause au tribunal inférieur avec la décision de la juridiction d’appel, sans reprendre l’ensemble des règles de procédure du renvoi.
correspondences.note_en: When the case is remanded to a trial court, the procedures applicable after cassation govern. Rule 84.28 and RSMo 512.160(5) authorize remand with the appellate decision, but do not set out the full procedure applicable to the remand.

correspondences.note_fr: La cour d'appel peut remplacer la décision attaquée par celle qu'elle estime devoir rendre, tandis que les autorités de première instance restent temporairement compétentes et doivent transmettre leurs décisions. Les Rules 84.14 et 512.160(3) couvrent le pouvoir de statuer à nouveau; la Rule 84.28 couvre le renvoi, mais pas le régime particulier de compétence et de transmission.
correspondences.note_en: The appellate court may substitute the judgment it considers proper, while the first-instance authorities retain limited competence and must transmit intervening decisions. Rules 84.14 and 512.160(3) cover appellate disposition, and Rule 84.28 covers remand, but none addresses the specific continuing jurisdiction and transmission mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: La Rule 84.28 permet le renvoi de l'affaire avec la décision de la cour. La Rule 84.16 exige la mise par écrit de la décision et la remise rapide d'une copie aux avocats des parties. Aucun texte ne prévoit ici la notification par le greffe ni le renvoi du dossier avec une copie certifiée conforme.
correspondences.note_en: Rule 84.28 permits remand of the case with the appellate decision. Rule 84.16 requires the decision to be written and a copy promptly furnished to counsel. Neither provision requires clerk notification or return of the record with a certified copy.

norms.heading: Claimant to Furnish Bond – Exception – Conditions of Bond

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
(a) Claimant to Furnish Bond. The claimant shall file a sufficient bond, approved by the court, executed by the claimant as principal and one or more sufficient sureties to the effect that they are bound to the State of Missouri in an amount set by the court but not exceeding double the amount claimed.

(b) Conditions of Bond. The conditions of the bond shall be that the claimant shall:

(1) Prosecute all claims without delay and with effect;

(2) Refund all sums of money that may be adjudged to be refunded to the owner of the property or found to have been received by the claimant and not justly due;

(3) Pay all damages and costs that may accrue to the owner of the property, any garnishee or interpleader by reason of the attachment, or any process or proceeding in the action, or by reason of any judgment or process thereon; and

(4) Pay all damages and costs that may accrue to any sheriff or other officer by reason of acting under the writ of attachment, following the instructions of the claimant.

(c) When No Bond Required. If the State or a county is a claimant in its own behalf no bond shall be required.

#### Committee Note – 1981

This is new.

Compare: Prior Rules 85.04, 85.06, 85.07 and 85.08.

norms.heading: Dissolution of Attachment

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
(a) Motion. Attachments may be dissolved on motion made by the owner of the property at any time before final judgment.

(b) Burden of Proof. The claimant shall have the burden of proving that the attachment was properly granted.

(c) When Attachment Dissolved. An attachment shall be dissolved at any time before final judgment when the court finds:

(1) The bond provided for in Rule 85.08 is inadequate and the claimant fails to file a sufficient bond, approved by the court, within such time as the court directs;

(2) The affidavit is insufficient and the claimant fails to file a sufficient affidavit, approved by the court, within such time as the court directs;

(3) The owner of the property has entered his appearance in the action and bond provided for in Rule 85.09 has been filed and approved; or

(4) For any other reason the writ of attachment should not have been issued.

#### Committee Note – 1981

This is new.

Compare: Prior Rules 85.39, 85.40 and 85.46.

norms.heading: Scope

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
In all condemnation proceedings, except those in instances where special provisions to the contrary are, or may hereafter be, provided for by charters or ordinances of those cities having constitutional charters, the procedure to be followed shall be that provided for by these rules.

#### Committee Note – 1959

Note:The rules relating to condemnation have been redrafted to provide for a single method of condemning property. Therefore there has been a grouping of some provisions from various sections. An attempt has been made to provide a fair procedure for all concerned. Provisions of constitutional charters and ordinances based thereon are not superseded because of the doubtful legality of action annulling constitutional charter provisions. Cities with Constitutional Charters may be subject to this Rule 86, by express adoption thereof or by the absence of special contrary provisions.

norms.heading: Parties

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
The individual or individuals, village trustees, corporation or organization, private or municipal, that has authority to bring a condemnation proceeding shall be the plaintiff or plaintiffs in such condemnation proceedings; the owners of any or all of the property that is to be condemned, or the use of which is to be condemned, or which will be benefited by an improvement involved in a condemnation proceeding, or who may have an interest therein may be made parties defendant. If the proceedings seek to affect the properties of persons under guardianship, the guardians must be made parties defendant. If the present owner of any land to be affected has a less estate than a fee, the person or persons having the next vested estate in reversion or in remainder and having future interest may, at the option of the petitioners, be made a party defendant; but, if any one having an interest in such property is not made a party, that person's interest shall not be bound by the proceedings. It shall not be necessary to make any persons parties defendants in respect to their ownership unless they are either (1) in actual possession of the property to be affected, claiming title or (2) have a title to the premises appearing of record upon the proper records of the county in which they lie. When legislation must be passed by a municipality before it is permitted to condemn property, it shall not be required in any case to bring any persons into the condemnation proceedings other than the owners of the property, or those interested therein, who were such at the time of the taking of effect of said legislation, and the parties claiming or holding through, or under, such owners, or parties interested, or any of them shall be bound by the proceedings as fully as if they were brought in.

#### Committee Note – 1959

Note:New.

Compare: Section 523.010, RSMo 1959.

(Amended September 28, 1993, effective January 1, 1994.)

norms.heading: Petition – Contents

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
The petition shall contain a description of the property or right which the plaintiff desires to acquire, use, or extinguish; if a dam is to be constructed across any watercourse, the petition shall contain the name of the watercourse, a description of the point at which it is desired to erect such dam and a description of any installations which it is proposed to erect in connection with the dam; the names of the owners of the property to be condemned, if known, or, if unknown, a statement that they are unknown; a statement of the foundation of the plaintiff's right to condemn the property involved in the condemnation proceedings; a general statement of the nature of the business, improvement or use for which the property is to be taken; a statement either that the condemner or owner can not agree on the proper compensation to be paid or that an owner is incapable of contracting, is unknown, can not be found or is a non-resident of the state; if any right of way be sought, the location and general route thereof shall be described and a copy of the construction plans required by Section 227.050 of the Revised Statutes of Missouri, 1949, shall be filed in the circuit clerk's office and made a part of each condemnation petition by reference; when property will be benefited by an improvement in connection with which condemnation proceedings are brought, a map of the benefit district involved, and a copy of any local legislation establishing the district shall be filed with the petition and made a part thereof; a prayer for the appointment of three disinterested freeholders, as commissioners, to assess the damages which such owners may severally sustain because of the condemnation of the property, and the use to which it is to be put and to assess benefits in those instances in which it is proper to make such assessments.

#### Committee Note – 1959

Note:New.

Compare: Section 523.010, RSMo 1959.

norms.heading: Appointment of Commissioners – Duties of – Standard for Damages

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
The court, or judge thereof in vacation, on being satisfied that due notice of the pendency of the petition has been given, shall appoint three disinterested commissioners, who shall be freeholders, resident of the county in which the real estate or a part thereof is situated, to assess the damages that the owners may severally sustain by reason of such appropriation.
The value of the property being condemned and all benefits and damages shall be assessed by said commissioners as of the date the assessment is made, and, if the award of said commissioners has not been paid to the defendants, or to the clerk of the court for said defendants, within one year after said commissioners' award is filed, any subsequent assessment of values, benefits and damages shall be as of the date of such subsequent assessment.
The commissioners, after having viewed the property, shall forthwith return, under oath, to the clerk of the court their report in duplicate setting forth, and stating separately as to all property held under the same ownership (1) the amount of net damages, if any, together with (2) a separate description of the property for which the damages are assessed.
The clerk shall file one of said copies in the clerk's office and cause the other to be delivered to the recorder for the county where the property lies, who shall record the same in the recorder's office and shall enter in the abstract and index of deeds at the proper place in the grantor's column the respective names of the first persons alleged to claim, or through whom is claimed some title to each of such respective separately described properties, and the fee for said recording shall be taxed by the clerk as costs of the proceedings.
When condemnation proceedings are brought in connection with a project to supply water to any city, town or village, the commissioners or jury shall inquire, and make report as to the value of the use of the stream, or the diversion of the waters thereof, to the extent to which the plaintiff proposes to use it, or to divert them, or what damage will be done by the erection and maintenance of any dam or buildings that it is proposed to erect and maintain in connection with aforesaid supplying of water, specifically stating to whom and upon what account damages are awarded.
When private property is appropriated by a municipality for any public place or use, resulting benefits shall be assessed against the municipality for the amount of the benefit to the public generally, and the balance of the benefits shall be assessed against the owner or owners having land within the benefit limits set by the municipality, which land shall be especially benefited by the proposed improvement, to the proportion that each lot of said owners shall be benefited.
Upon making payment to the clerk of the amount assessed, for the party or parties in whose favor such damages have been assessed, it shall be lawful for the condemner to take possession and hold the interest in the property so appropriated for the uses aforesaid;
and, upon failure to pay the assessment aforesaid within ten days after it becomes final or, in the case of a municipality, within thirty days thereafter, the court may, upon motion and notice by the party entitled to such damages, enforce the payment of the same by execution, unless the condemner shall, within said ten or thirty day period, elect to abandon the proposed appropriation of any property, by an instrument in writing to that effect, to be filed with the clerk of such court and entered on the minutes of the court, and to so much as is thus abandoned the assessment of damages shall be void.
If such appropriation be so abandoned as to any property, proceedings for the condemnation of the same property shall not be instituted again within two years after such abandonment. The report of the commissioners, when signed by two of said commissioners, shall be taken and considered as the report of all.

norms.heading: Who May Obtain Declaration of Rights or Other Legal Relations

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
(a) Persons Interested Under Deeds – Wills – Contracts – Statutes and the Like. Any person interested under a deed, will, written contract or other writings constituting a contract, or whose rights, status or other legal relations are affected by a statute, municipal ordinance, contract or franchise, may have determined any question of construction or validity arising under the instrument, statute, ordinance, contract or franchise and obtain a declaration of rights, status or other legal relations thereunder.
(b) Trusts, Infants, Lunatics, Incompetents. Any person interested as or through an executor, administrator, trustee, guardian or other fiduciary, creditor, devisee, legatee, heir, next of kin or

*cestui que*trust, in the administration of a trust, or of the estate of a decedent, an infant, lunatic or insolvent, may have a declaration of rights or legal relations in respect thereto:
(1) To ascertain any class of creditors, devisees, legatees, heirs, next of kin or others; or

(2) To direct the executors, administrators, or trustees to do or abstain from doing any particular act in their fiduciary capacity; or

(3) To determine any question arising in the administration of the estate or trust, including questions of construction of wills and other writings.
(c) Declaratory Judgment in Respect to Agency Rules. The power of the courts of this state to render declaratory judgments shall extend to declaratory judgments respecting the validity of agency rules, or of threatened applications thereof, and such suits may be maintained against agencies whether or not the plaintiff has first requested the agency to pass upon the question presented.
(d) Enumeration Not Exclusive. The foregoing enumeration of instances in which persons may obtain relief by declaratory judgments is illustrative, and anyone may obtain such relief in any instance in which it will terminate a controversy or remove an uncertainty.

The role of the mediator is to assist the parties in identifying the issues, reducing misunderstanding, clarifying priorities, exploring areas of compromise, and finding points of agreement. An agreement reached by the parties is to be based on the decisions of the parties and not the decisions of the mediator. The agreement reached can resolve all or only some of the contested issues.

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rule 88 — Domestic Relations and Paternity Cases – Calculation of Child Support – Mediation – Self-Represented Litigants

norms.text:
(a) The court may order mediation of any contested issue, including, but not limited to, child custody, parenting time, parenting plans, child support, maintenance, or property division, in domestic relations and paternity cases at any time upon the motion of a party or the court's own motion.

(b) No investigation and report will be ordered by the court during the pendency of the mediation.
(c) If the court orders mediation under this Rule, then the mediator shall meet the minimum qualifications required under Rule 88.05.

(d) The court may appoint a mediator agreed upon by the parties. If the parties cannot agree or if the court does not approve the agreed-upon mediator, the court may select the mediator.
(e) At any time following assignment of a mediator, a party may file a written application to disqualify the mediator for cause. A service copy of the application and a notice of the time when it will be presented to the court must be provided to all interested parties. Within 10 days of the application being filed, any adverse party may file a denial of the cause or causes alleged in the application.
If a denial is filed, the court may hear evidence and determine the issues. If the court finds in the applicant's favor or no denial is filed, reassignment of a mediator shall be done in accordance with the procedures for appointment of a mediator as set out in this Rule.

(f) To facilitate the use of mediation in domestic relations or paternity cases, circuits are encouraged to adopt local rules to accommodate and provide procedures for the use of mediation as may be ordered by the court or to provide for mandatory mediation within the circuit if desired. The Supreme Court of Missouri approved Model Local Rule 75 for this purpose.

correspondences.note_en: Rule 88.04 authorizes the court to order mediation, but it provides neither for reporting a party’s absence nor for a civil fine for unjustified noncompliance with the order.

correspondences.note_en: The French order must specify the neutral, mission, initial duration, return hearing, consent, and, for mediation, the advance and payment arrangements. correspondences.note_en: The conciliator or mediator has no investigative powers but may visit locations and hear persons with the parties’ and person’s consent. norms.heading: Mediation – Qualifications of the Mediator

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rule 88 — Domestic Relations and Paternity Cases – Calculation of Child Support – Mediation – Self-Represented Litigants

norms.text:
(a) A mediator who performs mediation in domestic relations and paternity cases pursuant to this Rule 88 shall be a person who has stated by affidavit that he or she:

(1) Is an attorney or a person who possesses a graduate degree in a field that includes the study of psychiatry, psychology, social work, counseling, or other behavioral science substantially related to marriage and family interpersonal relationships;
(2) Has received a minimum of 20 hours of child custody mediation training in a program approved by the court that shall include a component of training covering violence and power imbalance issues; and

(3) Any additional qualifications required by local court rule.
(b) Mediators qualified for appointment under this Rule may file proof of their qualifications with the circuit clerk of a county, who shall maintain a master list for the county of qualified mediators available for appointment. A circuit clerk's master list is not exhaustive of qualified mediators and does not prevent the appointment by the court of other qualified mediators under this Rule. Bar organizations may also maintain lists of qualified mediators.
(c) In appointing a qualified mediator, the court shall consider:

(1) The nature and extent of any relationship the mediator may have with the parties and any personal, financial, or other interests the mediator may have that could result in bias or conflict of interest; and
(2) The mediator's knowledge of: (A) the Missouri judicial system and the procedures used in domestic relations cases, (B) other resources in the community to which parties can be referred for assistance, (C) child development, (D) clinical issues relating to children, (E) the effects of the dissolution of marriage on children, (F) family systems theory, and (G) mediation and conflict resolution.

(a) At any time after two hours of mediation either party may terminate mediation ordered under Rule 88.04.

(b) The mediator shall terminate mediation whenever the mediator believes (1) that continuation of the process would harm or prejudice one or more of the parties or the children or (2) that the ability or willingness of any party to participate meaningfully in mediation is so lacking that a reasonable agreement is unlikely.
(c) The mediator shall report the termination of mediation to the court. The mediator shall not state the reason for termination except when the termination is due to a conflict of interest or bias on the part of the mediator, in which case another mediator may be appointed.

correspondences.note_fr: La convocation impose la comparution personnelle, règle l'assistance par avocat, prévoit une audience en chambre du conseil hors la présence du greffe et permet au juge d'y mettre fin. La Rule 55.29 autorise les actes en chambre sans greffe, tandis que la Rule 88.07 prévoit la cessation de la médiation, mais sans reprendre l'ensemble de ces modalités.
correspondences.note_en: The provision requires personal appearance, regulates attorney assistance, places the hearing in chambers without the clerk, and allows the judge to end it. Rule 55.29 permits proceedings in chambers without court officials, while Rule 88.07 addresses termination of mediation, but neither reproduces all of these arrangements.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe une durée maximale de cinq mois, avec une seule prolongation de trois mois. Les textes du Missouri prévoient plutôt la faculté ou l’obligation de mettre fin à la médiation après un certain temps ou nombre de séances, sans durée maximale comparable.
correspondences.note_en: The article sets an initial maximum of five months and permits one three-month extension. Missouri provisions instead allow or require termination after a specified period or number of sessions, without a comparable maximum duration.

correspondences.note_fr: Le conciliateur ou médiateur doit informer le juge des difficultés rencontrées ainsi que du succès ou de l’échec de la mesure. La Rule 88.07(c) exige seulement que le médiateur signale au tribunal la fin de la médiation, sans imposer d’information générale sur les difficultés ou le résultat.
correspondences.note_en: The conciliator or mediator must inform the judge of difficulties and of the success or failure of the process. Rule 88.07(c) only requires the mediator to report termination to the court; it imposes no general duty to report difficulties or the outcome.

correspondences.note_fr: Le juge peut mettre fin à la conciliation ou à la médiation à la demande d’une partie, du médiateur ou d’office lorsque son déroulement est compromis ou sans objet, puis faire reprendre l’instance. La Rule 88.07 permet aux parties ou au médiateur de mettre fin à la médiation dans certaines conditions et impose d’en informer le tribunal, mais ne confère pas le même pouvoir général au juge ni ne règle la reprise de l’instance.
correspondences.note_en: The judge may terminate conciliation or mediation at a party’s or mediator’s request, or on the judge’s own initiative when the process is compromised or pointless, with the case then resuming. Rule 88.07 permits termination by the parties or mediator under specified conditions and requires court notification, but lacks the CPC’s general judicial termination and resumption provisions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1536-3 règle l’interruption puis le nouveau départ du délai de péremption de l’instance pendant une conciliation ou une médiation, selon la date de son commencement et de sa fin. Les textes du Missouri organisent la terminaison de la médiation, mais ne prévoient aucun effet sur un délai de péremption.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1536-3 governs interruption and recommencement of the time limit for expiration of an action during conciliation or mediation. The Missouri provisions govern termination of mediation, but do not provide any effect on an action’s expiration period.

norms.heading: Confidentiality and Settlement

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rule 88 — Domestic Relations and Paternity Cases – Calculation of Child Support – Mediation – Self-Represented Litigants

norms.text:
(a) Mediation proceedings shall be regarded as settlement proceedings. With the exception of information released pursuant to Rule 88.06(a)(6), any communication relating to the subject matter of such disputes made during the mediation by any participant, mediator, or other person present at the mediation shall be a confidential communication. No admission, representation, statement, or other confidential communication made in setting up or conducting a mediation shall be admissible as evidence or subject to discovery except that no fact independently discoverable shall be immune from discovery by virtue of having been disclosed in such confidential communication.
(b) No person who serves as a mediator, nor any agent or employee of that person, shall be subpoenaed or otherwise compelled to disclose any matter disclosed in the process of setting up or conducting the mediation.

(c) All mediations shall be non-binding unless the parties enter into a written agreement as provided in Rule 88.08(d). A written agreement shall be binding to the extent not prohibited by law.
(d) Settlement shall be by a written document setting out the essential terms of the agreement executed after the mediation's termination.

(e) An individual or organization providing mediation services pursuant to this Rule 88 or any agent or employee of the individual or organization may be called in an action to enforce the written settlement agreement reached following the mediation's conclusion for the limited purpose of describing events following the mediation's conclusion.
