correspondences.note_fr: Le juge contribue à la conciliation, détermine avec les parties le mode amiable adapté et les parties peuvent régler tout ou partie du litige à tout moment. Les dispositions du Missouri organisent la médiation et les accords amiables, mais principalement pour les affaires familiales et selon des conditions plus limitées.
correspondences.note_en: The judge facilitates conciliation, determines the appropriate amicable-resolution method with the parties, and the parties may settle all or part of the dispute at any time. Missouri provisions govern mediation and settlements, but mainly in domestic-relations cases and subject to narrower conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 281 prévoit qu’en cas de conciliation pendant l’expertise, l’expert constate que sa mission est devenue sans objet et en informe le juge; les parties peuvent demander que leur accord reçoive force exécutoire. La Rule 88.08 organise un accord écrit issu d’une médiation et son exécution, tandis que les deux sections RSMo prévoient, dans des contextes particuliers, l’approbation ou l’exécution judiciaire d’un règlement.
correspondences.note_en: Article 281 provides that, when the parties settle during the expert process, the expert reports that the mission has become moot; the parties may ask the judge to make their agreement enforceable. Rule 88.08 governs a written mediation settlement and its enforcement, while the two RSMo sections provide court approval or judgment enforcement of settlements in specialized contexts.

correspondences.note_fr: Le conseiller de la mise en état veille à la loyauté et au calendrier de la procédure, peut ordonner une conciliation ou une médiation et homologuer l’accord soumis par les parties. La Rule 88.04 permet au tribunal d’ordonner une médiation, mais seulement dans les affaires familiales et de paternité; la Rule 88.08 encadre l’accord écrit issu de la médiation sans prévoir une homologation générale.
correspondences.note_en: The French rule assigns case-management duties, permits court-directed conciliation or mediation, and allows homologation of a settlement. Rule 88.04 permits court-ordered mediation only in domestic-relations and paternity cases, while Rule 88.08 governs the resulting written settlement but does not provide a general homologation mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1189-1 prévoit la médiation familiale ordonnée par le juge, les qualifications du médiateur, la participation éventuelle de l’enfant et l’homologation de l’accord. Les Rules 88.04 à 88.08 règlent la médiation familiale, les qualifications, l’audition de l’enfant et l’accord écrit, mais dans le cadre plus général des affaires familiales et de la paternité.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1189-1 provides for court-ordered family mediation, mediator qualifications, possible participation by the child, and approval of the resulting agreement. Rules 88.04–88.08 address court-ordered family mediation, qualifications, meetings with children, and written settlements, but under the broader framework of domestic-relations and paternity cases.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article pose une confidentialité générale pour l’audience de règlement amiable, la conciliation et la médiation, avec des exceptions et un régime particulier pour les pièces et l’exécution de l’accord. La Rule 88.08 protège largement les communications de médiation et encadre l’accord écrit, mais ne couvre ni toutes les procédures ni toutes les exceptions françaises.
correspondences.note_en: The article establishes broad confidentiality for settlement hearings, conciliation, and mediation, with exceptions and special treatment of documents and enforcement. Rule 88.08 broadly protects mediation communications and regulates written settlements, but does not cover all procedures or all French exceptions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article applique à la réunion d’information les règles de confidentialité et précise que la présence ou l’absence d’une partie n’est pas confidentielle. La Rule 88.06 impose une information sur le processus, et la Rule 88.08 régit la confidentialité de la médiation, sans prévoir expressément cette règle pour une réunion d’information.
correspondences.note_en: The article applies confidentiality rules to the information meeting while expressly excluding a party’s attendance or absence from confidentiality. Rule 88.06 addresses explaining the mediation process, and Rule 88.08 governs mediation confidentiality, but neither expressly establishes this attendance rule for an information meeting.

correspondences.note_fr: Le CPC prévoit la constatation écrite de l’accord de conciliation ou de médiation, avec des signatures déterminées et, pour la médiation, une attestation du médiateur. Le Missouri exige également un accord écrit pour le règlement, mais impose des conditions supplémentaires, notamment la signature des avocats ou l’approbation du tribunal selon le cas.
correspondences.note_en: The CPC provides for a written record of a conciliation or mediation agreement, with specified signatures and, for mediation, the mediator’s certification of its origin. Missouri likewise requires a written settlement, but adds conditions such as attorney signatures or court approval depending on the case.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1536-4 renvoie aux règles relatives à l’établissement de l’accord issu d’une conciliation ou médiation conventionnelle. Les Rules 88.08 et 88.06 exigent également une formalisation écrite de l’accord, mais dans le cadre de médiations de droit familial et avec des conditions propres, notamment la signature et l’approbation judiciaire.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1536-4 refers to the rules governing the preparation of an agreement resulting from conventional conciliation or mediation. Rules 88.08 and 88.06 likewise require a written settlement, but apply to domestic-relations mediation and impose distinct conditions, including signatures and court approval.

correspondences.note_fr: L’accord total ou partiel doit être constaté dans un acte sous signature privée. La Rule 88.08(d) exige un document écrit exposant les conditions essentielles du règlement après la médiation, mais ne prévoit pas expressément les formalités de signature privée de l’article français.
correspondences.note_en: A settlement resolving all or part of the dispute must be recorded in a privately signed instrument. Rule 88.08(d) requires a written document stating the settlement’s essential terms after mediation, but does not expressly provide the French article’s private-signature formalities.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article pose le régime général de l’accord amiable : formation par échange des consentements, écrit et éventuelle force exécutoire. La Rule 88.08 et les RSMo 452.325 et 511.740-511.750 prévoient des accords écrits ou des soumissions et leur exécution, mais dans des cadres plus spécifiques.
correspondences.note_en: The article establishes a general regime for amicable agreements: formation by consent, possible written form, and enforceability. Rule 88.08 and RSMo 452.325 and 511.740-511.750 address written settlements or submissions and enforcement, but only in more specific settings.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise la reconnaissance et la déclaration de force exécutoire en France d’un accord de médiation déjà rendu exécutoire dans un autre État membre de l’Union européenne. La Rule 74.14 et les RSMo 511.778-511.780 concernent la reconnaissance et l’exécution de jugements étrangers, tandis que la Rule 88.08 vise l’exécution d’un accord écrit de médiation, sans mécanisme spécifique de reconnaissance transfrontière.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides for recognition and enforcement in France of a mediated settlement already made enforceable in another EU Member State. Rule 74.14 and RSMo 511.778-511.780 address recognition and enforcement of foreign judgments, while Rule 88.08 concerns enforcement of a written mediation settlement without a specific cross-border recognition mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1543 permet de faire homologuer un accord issu notamment d’une médiation afin de lui conférer force exécutoire, y compris l’accord sur la rémunération du médiateur dans une médiation ordonnée. Les Rules 88.06 et 88.08 exigent un accord écrit et, pour la médiation familiale, son approbation judiciaire ou permettent son exécution, mais ne prévoient pas une procédure générale d’homologation équivalente.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1543 permits court homologation of an agreement resulting from mediation, conciliation, or participatory proceedings so that it becomes enforceable, including a mediator-fee agreement in court-ordered mediation. Rules 88.06 and 88.08 require a written agreement and, in domestic-relations mediation, court approval or enforcement, but do not establish an equivalent general homologation procedure.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article permet au greffe d'apposer la formule exécutoire sur certains accords écrits, après vérification de sa compétence et de la nature de l'acte. La règle 88.08 prévoit qu'un règlement écrit issu d'une médiation est obligatoire et peut être exécuté, tandis que les §§ 511.740 et 511.750 organisent la soumission judiciaire d'une controverse et l'exécution du jugement, sans mécanisme identique d'apposition par le greffe.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows the clerk to make specified written settlements enforceable after checking jurisdiction and the instrument's nature. Rule 88.08 makes a written mediated settlement binding and enforceable, while §§ 511.740 and 511.750 provide judicial submission and enforcement of a resulting judgment, but none creates the same clerk-certification mechanism.

norms.heading: Parties Not Represented By Counsel

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rule 88 — Domestic Relations and Paternity Cases – Calculation of Child Support – Mediation – Self-Represented Litigants

norms.text:
Every party not represented by counsel who participates in a proceeding for dissolution of marriage, legal separation, parentage or the modification of a judgment in any such proceeding shall:

(a) Complete a litigant awareness program that includes an explanation of the risks and responsibilities of self-representation, unless waived by the circuit court. The awareness program shall be prepared by a committee designated by this Court, but each circuit may determine the manner and means by which the training shall be provided and the proof of compliance; and
(b) Unless such use is waived by the trial court, use the pleadings, forms, and proposed judgment prepared by a committee designated by this Court that have been approved by this Court. These forms shall be accepted by the courts of this state, until disapproved or superseded by this Court.

(c) Nothing in this Rule 88.09 prevents a court from determining the legal sufficiency of any pleading nor prevents a court from entering judgment in a form different from the judgment form approved pursuant to Rule 88.09(b).

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 18 autorise l’auto-défense, sauf lorsque la représentation est obligatoire. La Rule 55.03 permet à une partie non représentée de signer ses actes de procédure et lui impose certaines certifications, tandis que la Rule 88.09 impose des obligations particulières aux parties non représentées dans certaines affaires familiales. Aucune ne pose la règle générale de l’article 18.
correspondences.note_en: Article 18 permits self-representation unless representation is mandatory. Rule 55.03 allows a self-represented party to sign filings and imposes certifications, while Rule 88.09 imposes special duties on unrepresented parties in specified domestic-relations proceedings. Neither establishes Article 18’s general rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 761 énumère les cas de dispense de constitution d'avocat, notamment selon la matière et le montant, et prévoit certaines modalités de représentation des personnes publiques. Rule 55.03 reconnaît la partie se représentant elle-même et Rule 88.09 organise cette situation dans certaines affaires familiales, sans reprendre les dispenses ni les seuils français.
correspondences.note_en: Article 761 lists exemptions from mandatory counsel, including matter- and amount-based exemptions, and addresses representation of public entities. Rule 55.03 recognizes self-representation and Rule 88.09 regulates it in certain domestic-relations matters, but neither reproduces the French exemptions or monetary thresholds.

correspondences.note_fr: L'article 762 autorise l'autodéfense et la représentation par l'avocat ou par certaines personnes non avocates, sous réserve d'un pouvoir spécial. Rule 55.03 concerne les actes signés par une partie se représentant elle-même, tandis que Rule 88.09 organise l'autoreprésentation dans certaines affaires familiales. RSMo 210.153 concerne une procédure de réexamen en matière de protection de l'enfance et ne constitue pas une règle générale de représentation.
correspondences.note_en: Article 762 permits self-representation and representation by counsel or specified nonlawyers, subject to a special power. Rule 55.03 addresses filings by self-represented parties, while Rule 88.09 regulates self-representation in specified domestic-relations proceedings. RSMo 210.153 concerns child-abuse review proceedings and is not a general representation rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet aux parties de se défendre elles-mêmes ou d’être assistées ou représentées, avec un pouvoir spécial pour le représentant non avocat. La Rule 84.01 reconnaît la signature par une partie non représentée, tandis que la Rule 88.09 encadre spécifiquement les parties sans avocat dans certaines affaires familiales.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows parties to appear on their own or to be assisted or represented, requiring a special authorization for a non-lawyer representative. Rule 84.01 recognizes filing by a self-represented party, while Rule 88.09 regulates self-represented parties specifically in certain domestic-relations proceedings.

correspondences.note_fr: La Rule 88.09 concerne les parties non représentées dans certaines procédures de droit familial ; les Rules 55.03 et 55.035 concernent respectivement la signature des actes et l’intervention de l’avocat. Aucun de ces textes ne prévoit une obligation d’avocat comparable à celle exigée pour la révision d’une prestation compensatoire.
correspondences.note_en: Rule 88.09 addresses self-represented parties in specified domestic-relations proceedings; Rules 55.03 and 55.035 address signatures and counsel appearances. None of these Missouri provisions states a counsel requirement comparable to the French rule for modification of a compensatory award.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article garantit que les parties peuvent se défendre elles-mêmes ou être représentées par un mandataire, sans représentation obligatoire. Le Missouri prévoit l’auto-représentation surtout en matière familiale et encadre l’intervention et le retrait des avocats, sans règle générale identique.
correspondences.note_en: The article guarantees that parties may appear pro se or through a representative, without mandatory representation. Missouri addresses self-representation mainly in domestic-relations cases and regulates attorney appearances and withdrawal, but supplies no identical general rule.

norms.heading: Service on Garnishee – Return of Service – Return Date – Notice to Judgment Debtor – Service of Subsequent Pleadings and Papers

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
(a) The garnishee shall be served with summons and the writ of garnishment by the sheriff. If the sheriff fails to obtain service upon a request to do so, the garnishor may request the court to appoint a special process server. The special process server shall have the same duties as the sheriff with respect to service of garnishments.
In addition, service may be made upon an employee of the garnishee designated to receive service or upon the paying, disbursing, or auditing officer of the garnishee. Return of service shall be made as provided in Rule 54.20. The return date of the writ of garnishment, if applicable, shall be set forth in the summons.
(b) Within five days of notice of service upon the garnishee, the garnishor shall serve a copy of the summons and writ on the judgment debtor by delivering it to the judgment debtor as provided in Rule 43.01(c) or by mailing the documents to the debtor’s last known address. Service by mail shall be complete upon mailing. At the time of mailing, a certificate of service shall be filed with the court. The certificate shall show the caption of the case, the name of the party served, the date and manner of service, the designation of the documents, and the signature of the serving party or attorney.
(c) Within five days of service of the summons and writ upon the garnishee, the garnishee shall hand deliver or mail a copy of the summons and writ on the judgment debtor at debtor’s last known address according to the garnishee’s records.

(d) All pleadings and papers subsequent to service of the summons and writ of garnishment shall be served as provided in Rule 43.01.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe, pour les notifications effectuées hors de certains territoires ou à l’étranger, la date d’expédition comme date de notification à l’égard de l’expéditeur, avec une règle subsidiaire de réception par le parquet. La Rule 90.03(b) prévoit que certains envois sont accomplis dès leur expédition, tandis que les autres textes organisent surtout la preuve de la signification hors de l’État, sans fixer une règle générale de computation.
correspondences.note_en: The article treats the dispatch date as the notification date, for the sender, when service is made in specified overseas territories or abroad, with a fallback based on receipt by the competent public prosecutor. Rule 90.03(b) makes certain mailed service complete upon mailing, while the other provisions mainly govern proof of out-of-state service and do not establish a general computation rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose un avis postal supplémentaire le jour même ou le premier jour ouvrable, avec copie de l’acte, après certaines significations. Les textes Missouri prévoient des notifications postérieures par courrier dans des contextes particuliers, notamment après signification à un fonctionnaire ou en matière de saisie-arrêt, mais pas une règle générale identique.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires an additional postal notice, generally the same day or next business day, with a copy of the document, after specified forms of service. Missouri provides comparable post-service notices in specific settings—service through officials and garnishment—but no identical general rule.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article fixe, pour la notification postale, une date d’expédition pour l’auteur et une date de réception pour le destinataire. Rule 90.03(b) rend le service par courrier parfait lors de l’envoi, tandis que Rule 54.16 rattache certains délais à la date d’envoi, sans établir la règle générale française.
correspondences.note_en: The article assigns the mailing date to the sender and the receipt date to the recipient. Rule 90.03(b) makes service by mail complete upon mailing, while Rule 54.16 measures a consequence from mailing, but neither establishes the French general two-sided rule.

norms.heading: Effect of Service of Writ of Garnishment and Summons

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
The service of the writ of garnishment and summons attaches the property subject to garnishment in the garnishee's possession or charge or under the garnishee's control at the time the writ of garnishment and summons is served and continuing through the return date of the writ or, in the case of a continuous wage garnishment, until the judgment is paid in full or until the employment relationship is terminated, whichever occurs first.
Writs of garnishment that would otherwise have equal priority shall have priority according to the date of service on the garnishee. If the employee's wages have been attached by more than one writ of garnishment, the employer shall inform the inferior garnishor of the existence and case number of all senior garnishments.

norms.heading: Request for Immediate Delivery of Property to Sheriff – Order of Delivery

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
(a) When the garnishor requests an order requiring immediate delivery to the sheriff of property subject to garnishment, the garnishor shall file an affidavit stating:

(1) the description of the property;

(2) facts showing the reason that immediate delivery to the sheriff should be made; and

(3) the garnishor is in danger of losing the property unless immediate delivery to the sheriff is made.

norms.heading: Interrogatories to Garnishee – Answers to Interrogatories – Exceptions – Response

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
(a) Interrogatories – Time for Service. The garnishor shall serve written interrogatories simultaneously with the garnishment asking the garnishee to:

(1) List and describe the property subject to garnishment in the possession, charge, or control of the garnishee and, in the case of a wage garnishment, state the gross amount of earnings, as defined in section 525.030, RSMo, due to the debtor and the nonexempt portion of such earnings subject to garnishment;
(2) State the last known address of the debtor and the name and last known address of any person, other than debtor, whom the garnishee knows claims or may claim an interest in or to the property subject to garnishment;

(3) If the garnishee is a bank or other financial institution, state whether at the time the writ of garnishment was served or at any subsequent time did the debtor have funds on deposit in an account in which all funds are:
(A) Deposited electronically on a recurring basis, and

(B) Reasonably identified as being funds on deposit that are exempt from garnishment pursuant to section 513.430.1(10)(a), (b), or (c), RSMo, or subject to the exemptions under Title 31 C.F.R. Part 212. If such funds are on deposit, the garnishee shall identify each account, state the reason for the believed exemption, and identify the entity electronically depositing those funds;
(4) Identify the existence and case number of all senior garnishments and inform the garnishor upon the release, satisfaction, or termination of a senior garnishment; and

(5) Notify the garnishor upon termination of the judgment debtor’s employment. Supplementation of interrogatory responses shall be a continuing duty of the garnishee so long as the garnishment remains in effect.
Supplementation of interrogatory responses shall be a continuing duty of the garnishee so long as the garnishment remains in effect.

The interrogatories shall be served simultaneously with the summons and writ of garnishment. The garnishor shall provide the interrogatories to the serving officer after the issued summons and writ have been returned to the garnishor by the court.
(b) Answer to Interrogatories – Time for Filing. The garnishee shall file and serve verified answers to the interrogatories on the garnishor during the ten days immediately after the return date of the writ or, in the case of a continuous wage garnishment, within 20 days from the date on which the garnishee is served with the writ.
(c) Exceptions to Answers to Interrogatories – Time for Filing. The garnishor shall file and serve on the garnishee any exceptions to the interrogatory answers, asserting any objections to the answers and asserting all grounds upon which recovery is sought against the garnishee.

The exceptions shall be filed within the later of:
(1) 20 days after service of the answers, or

(2) 20 days after the return date of the writ.

In the case of a continuous wage garnishment, the exceptions shall be filed not later than 20 days after service of the answers.

The garnishee's answers to interrogatories are conclusively binding against the garnishor if the garnishor does not timely file exceptions to the interrogatory answers.
(d) Response to Exceptions – Time for Filing. Within 20 days after service of the exceptions, the garnishee may file a response thereto.
(e) Filing. Interrogatories under this Rule 90.07 shall not be filed with the court except upon court order or contemporaneously with exceptions placing the interrogatory answers in issue. However, both when the interrogatories and answers are served, the party serving them shall file with the court a certificate of service. The certificate shall show the caption of the case, the name of the party served, the date and manner of service, the designation of the document, e.g., first interrogatories or answers to second interrogatories, and the signature of the serving party or attorney.

norms.heading: Cost and Allowances

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
(a) Allowance to Garnishee if Interrogatory Answers are Not Excepted to or Denied. If by interrogatory answers not excepted to or denied it appears that the garnishee has property subject to garnishment, the garnishee may deduct a one-time sum not to exceed $20, or the fee previously agreed upon between the garnishee and the judgment debtor if the garnishee is a financial institution, for the trouble and expense of answering and withholding the funds to be paid out of the property subject to garnishment.
The fee shall not be a credit against the court-ordered judgment and shall be collected first. The garnishee may file a motion for additional cost, including attorney fees reasonably incurred in answering the interrogatories, in which case the court may make such award as it deems reasonable. The motion shall be filed on or before the date the garnishee makes payment or delivers the property subject to garnishment into court.
(b) Allowance to Garnishee if Garnishor Does Not Recover Judgment Against Garnishee. If the garnishor files exceptions to the garnishee's interrogatory answers but does not obtain a judgment against the garnishee, all of the costs attending such garnishment shall be taxed against the garnishor.
The court in such a case shall render judgment in favor of the garnishee and against the garnishor for an amount sufficient to reimburse the garnishee for time and expenses, including attorney fees reasonably incurred. The fact that the garnishee affirmatively asserted in good faith an exemption belonging to the judgement debtor shall not deprive the garnishee of the right to costs and attorney fees as otherwise provided herein.
(c) Allowance to Garnishee in Appellate Court. A garnishee claiming an allowance in an appellate court shall do so pursuant to Rule 84.21.

norms.heading: Reporting Judgment Balance – Remaining Due – Payment on the Record

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
(a) A judgment creditor may, prior to the expiration of a judgment, file a statement of judgment balance remaining due with the court, and any payment referenced in the statement shall be deemed a payment on the record for the purposes of section 516.350, RSMo. The statement of judgment balance remaining due shall show the amount still owed to the judgment creditor as of a date certain. Copies of the statement shall be served by ordinary mail on the judgment debtor. A statement filed pursuant to this Rule 90.19(a) shall renew the six month filing requirement of Rule 90.19(b), if applicable.
(b) In the case of a continuous wage garnishment or in any case in which the garnishor has elected to have payments made directly to its attorney pursuant to Rule 90.02(e), the garnishor shall file with the issuing court a statement of judgment balance remaining due. The statement shall indicate all payments received by the garnishor within the preceding six months and the remaining unsatisfied portions of the judgment, which may include all unsatisfied post-judgment interest and costs.
The statement shall be filed not later than 20 days after the close of each such six-month period. The statement shall be filed with the issuing court beginning six months after issuance of the garnishment and shall continue every six months thereafter until the garnishment is satisfied or no longer effective. Copies of the statement shall be served by ordinary mail on the garnishee and judgment debtor.
In the case of garnishment other than a continuous wage garnishment in which the garnishor has elected to have payments made directly to its attorney pursuant to Rule 90.02(e), a statement of judgment balance need not be filed if the garnishor files a new garnishment in the same case and against the same defendant prior to the date the statement would have been required to be filed with the issuing court.
(c) If a garnishor fails to file a statement of judgment balance remaining due as provided in Rule 90.19(b), the court shall, upon its own motion or that of any party or junior garnishor, terminate the garnishment.

(d) Any party may file with the issuing court a motion for accounting of judgment balance up to 30 days after satisfaction of the judgment.
(e) As to any garnishment in effect when the judgment is no longer enforceable for any reason, whether due to satisfaction, accord, setting aside the judgment, reversal on appeal, or otherwise, the garnishor shall provide notice in writing to the garnishee not later than 20 days after such event or occurrence. Any final remittance from the garnishee that exceeds the amount necessary to fully satisfy the judgment, shall be returned within 10 days to the garnishee.

norms.heading: Exemptions

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
(a) Every writ of garnishment shall have clearly and legibly printed thereon a notice to the person against whom the garnishment has issued that:

(1) A garnishment has been levied;

(2) Certain funds may be exempt under sections 513.430 and 513.440, RSMo, or under Title 31 C.F.R. Part 212; and
(3) The person has the right to hold the funds as exempt from garnishment.

The notice shall also generally state that there are certain exemptions under state and federal law that the judgment debtor may be able to claim with respect to the funds levied upon and describe the procedure for claiming the funds as exempt.
(b) The judgment debtor may claim any exemption by filing a verified claim of exemption with the court and serving a copy of it on the garnishor within 20 days after being served with the notice of garnishment. The party requesting the garnishment may object to any claim for exemption within 20 days of the filing of the verified request by filing a request for court review.
If a request for court review is not timely filed, the garnishee shall release from garnishment the funds claimed as exempt by the judgment debtor or, if any such exempt funds shall have been previously paid to the court or the garnishor, such exempt funds shall be returned to the judgment debtor not later than ten days after the last day on which the garnishor could have timely filed a request for court review.
(c) Upon filing of an objection to a claim of exemption, the clerk shall promptly present said objection before the court in chambers. The court may rule upon the objection to claim of exemption upon the pleadings or may order a hearing. Any hearing required by the court shall be expedited, shall be held not later than 30 days after the filing of the request for court review, and shall be held upon not less than five days notice of the hearing to all parties in interest.

norms.heading: Habeas Corpus – General – Who May Petition for – Forms of Action

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
(a) Proceedings in habeas corpus in a circuit court shall be as prescribed in this Rule 91 and in this Court or the court of appeals shall be as prescribed in Rule 84.22 to 84.26, inclusive, and this Rule 91. In all particulars not provided for by the foregoing provisions, proceedings in habeas corpus shall be governed by and conform to the rules of civil procedure and the existing rules of general law upon the subject. The court may, by order, direct the form of such further details of procedure as may be necessary to the orderly course of the action to give effect to the remedy.
(b) Any person restrained of liberty within this state may petition for a writ of habeas corpus to inquire into the cause of such restraint. Custody of a child may be the subject of a proceeding in habeas corpus.

(c) A habeas corpus proceeding shall be a civil action in which the person seeking relief is petitioner and the person against whom such relief is sought is respondent. If appropriate, there may be multiple petitioners or multiple respondents.

#### Committee Note – 1983

The source is prior Rule 91.01.

The second sentence concerning the custody of children being the subject of habeas corpus is not intended to change existing law as to when the remedy is available but has been added simply to call attention to the fact that the remedy may be available in certain situations.

Prior Rule 91.60 purports to give a habeas corpus remedy in child custody cases but there are not any reported cases that fit the very limited factual situation described in that rule. The remedy of habeas corpus in child custody cases has developed independent of statute or rule.
Prior Rule 91.60 has been deleted because it is misleading and is so narrow in scope that it is meaningless.

A habeas corpus action shall be styled in the name of the person whose liberty or custody is to be affected and the names of the petitioner and respondent thus:

In re ____________________

___________________, Petitioner
vs.

____________________, Respondent

See Rule 24.035 and Rule 29.15 for the exclusive remedy in certain situations.

(Rule adopted June 24, 1982, effective January 1, 1983. Amended September 28, 1993, effective January 1, 1994; amended October 22, 1996, effective July 1, 1997.)
(Committee note amended February 20, 1987, effective January 1, 1988.)

norms.heading: Petition to What Court First Made

(a) Except as provided in subdivision (b) of this Rule 91.02, when a person who is held in custody on a charge of crime seeks the benefit of this Rule 91, the petition in the first instance shall be to a circuit or associate circuit judge for the county in which the person is held in custody if at the time of the petition such judge is in the county, unless good cause is shown for filing the petition in a higher court. The petitioner shall give reasonable notice of the time and place of filing the petition to the prosecuting attorney for the county in which the petition is to be filed, if at the time thereof the attorney is in the county. Upon such notice, the attorney shall attend the hearing of the petition on behalf of the state.

The petitioner shall give reasonable notice of the time and place of filing the petition to the attorney general of this state, who shall represent the state in the matter. Any such petition filed in a state court other than this Court shall be deemed to have been filed in this Court. Any clerk filing such a petition shall give notice for the filing of the petition to the clerk of this Court by telephone or by other expeditious means and shall forward the petition to this Court immediately.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 834 permet au président du tribunal judiciaire d’ordonner en urgence toute mesure non sérieusement contestable ou justifiée par un différend. La Rule 92.02 prévoit des mesures injonctives provisoires en cas de préjudice immédiat et irréparable, mais avec des conditions, une procédure et des effets différents; la Rule 92.01 désigne les juges compétents.
correspondences.note_en: Article 834 permits the president of the judicial court to order urgent relief where there is no serious dispute or where a dispute warrants it. Rule 92.02 provides provisional injunctive relief for immediate and irreparable harm, but under materially different conditions, procedures, and effects; Rule 92.01 identifies the authorized judges.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 872 permet au président du tribunal de commerce, en urgence, d’ordonner toute mesure provisoire non sérieusement contestée ou justifiée par un différend. La Rule 92.02 encadre les injonctions et mesures de restraint d’urgence, mais selon des conditions, une procédure et des effets différents ; la Rule 92.01 concerne le pouvoir de les accorder.
correspondences.note_en: Article 872 authorizes the president of the commercial court to order urgent interim measures when they face no serious challenge or are justified by a dispute. Rule 92.02 governs emergency restraining and injunctive relief, but with different conditions, procedures, and effects; Rule 92.01 addresses judicial authority to grant injunctions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 873 vise les mesures conservatoires ou de remise en état en cas de dommage imminent ou de trouble manifestement illicite, ainsi que la provision lorsque l’obligation n’est pas sérieusement contestable. La Rule 92.02 couvre principalement les mesures injonctives d’urgence ; la Rule 68.02 permet la préservation de biens par un receiver, sans prévoir la provision française.
correspondences.note_en: Article 873 covers protective or restorative measures for imminent harm or manifestly unlawful interference, and provisional payment or performance when the obligation is not seriously disputed. Rule 92.02 chiefly addresses emergency injunctive relief; Rule 68.02 permits preservation of property through a receiver, but does not provide the French-style provisional award.

norms.heading: Temporary Restraining Order – Notice – Preliminary Injunction – Bond – Form and Scope

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
(a) Temporary Restraining Order – With Notice.

(1) When Issued. The court shall not grant a temporary restraining order unless the party seeking relief demonstrates that immediate and irreparable injury, loss, or damage will result in the absence of relief.

(2) Proof Required. A party seeking a temporary restraining order shall support that request with a verified petition or affidavit reciting the specific facts that support the showing required by Rule 92.02(a)(1).
(3) Required Notice. Except as provided in Rule 92.02(b), no temporary restraining order shall issue without reasonable notice at least twenty-four hours before the hearing on the motion to the party against whom relief is sought.

(4) Form. A temporary restraining order shall be endorsed with the date and hour of issuance, shall be filed forthwith in the clerk's office and entered of record, and shall set forth specific facts that support the showing required by Rule 92.02(a)(1).
(5) Duration. A temporary restraining order shall expire within such time after entry, not to exceed fifteen days, as the court fixes. The court may extend the order for additional periods, not to exceed fifteen days each, if the party seeking relief shows that the grounds specified in Rule 92.02(a)(1) continue to exist.
(b) Temporary Restraining Order – Without Notice.

(1) When Issued. A party seeking a temporary restraining order without notice shall make the showing required under Rule 92.02(a). The court shall not grant a temporary restraining order without prior notice to the party against whom relief is sought unless the party seeking relief establishes that notice cannot be given or notice would defeat the purpose of the order.
(2) Proof Required. A party seeking a temporary restraining order without notice shall file a verified petition or affidavit reciting the specific facts that support the showing required by Rule 92.02(b)(1).

(3) Form. A temporary restraining order granted without notice shall be endorsed with the date and hour of issuance, shall be filed forthwith in the clerk's office and entered of record, and shall set forth specific facts that support the showing required by Rule 92.02(b)(1). A temporary restraining order failing to set forth such specific facts is void
ab initio.

(4) Duration. A temporary restraining order granted without notice shall expire within such time after entry, not to exceed ten days, as the court fixes. The court may extend the order for additional periods, not to exceed ten days each, after notice to the party against whom relief is sought. The court may dispense with such notice only if the party seeking relief establishes that notice cannot be given to the party against whom relief is sought or notice would defeat the purpose of the order.
(5) When Set Aside. On one day's notice to the party who obtained the temporary restraining order without notice, or on such shorter notice as the court may prescribe, the adverse party may appear and move to dissolve or modify the order. At the hearing, the burden shall be upon the party seeking the temporary restraining order to establish a right to relief.
(6) Sanction for Failure to Provide Required Notice. If the court finds that a party obtaining a temporary restraining order without notice did not have a reasonable basis to proceed without notice, the party shall be presumed to have acted in bad faith and to have violated Rule 55.03(c). The thirty-day provisions of Rule 55.03(d)(1)(A) shall not apply to proceedings under this Rule 92.02(b)(6).
(c) Preliminary Injunction.

(1) Notice. A preliminary injunction shall not issue unless the party against whom relief is sought is given prior notice and an opportunity to be heard.

(2) Time. If a temporary restraining order is in effect for more than thirty days without a hearing on an application for a preliminary injunction, the court shall schedule a hearing at the earliest possible date. The hearing shall take precedence over all other matters except older matters of the same character. The hearing on the application for a preliminary injunction may be delayed past these limits if all parties consent.
(3) Consolidation With Hearing on the Merits. At any time the court may order the trial of the action on the merits to be advanced and consolidated with the hearing of the application for a preliminary injunction. Any evidence received upon an application for a preliminary injunction admissible at the trial on the merits becomes part of the trial record and need not be repeated at the trial. This Rule 92.02(c)(3) shall be so construed and applied to preserve any party's right to trial by jury.
(d) Bond.
No injunction or temporary restraining order, unless on final hearing or judgment, shall issue in any case, except in suits instituted by the state in its own behalf, until the plaintiff, or some responsible person for the plaintiff, shall have executed a bond with sufficient surety or sureties to the other party, in such
sum as the court shall deem sufficient to secure the amount or other matter to be enjoined, and all damages that may be occasioned by such injunction or temporary restraining order to the parties enjoined, or to any party interested in the subject matter of the controversy, conditioned that the plaintiff will abide by the decision that shall be made thereon and pay all sums of money, damages and costs that shall be adjudged if the injunction or temporary restraining order shall be dissolved. In lieu of the bond the plaintiff may deposit with the court such sum, in cash, as the court may require sufficient to secure such amount.
(e) Form and Scope of Injunction or Temporary Restraining Order. Every order granting an injunction and every restraining order shall set forth the reasons for its issuance; shall be specific in terms; shall describe in reasonable detail, and not by reference to the petition or other document, the act or acts sought to be restrained; and is binding only upon the parties to the action, their officers, agents, servants, employees, and attorneys, and upon those persons in active concert or participation with them who receive actual notice of the order by personal service or otherwise.

#### Committee Note – 1981

Paragraph (a) is the same as Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(a).

Paragraph (b) is the same as Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(b).

Compare: Prior Rules 92.02, 92.16 and 92.19.

Paragraph (c) is the same as prior Rule 92.09 except that "temporary" has been added before "restraining order."
Paragraph (d) is the same as Fed. R. Civ. P. 65(d).

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 14 interdit qu’une partie soit jugée sans avoir été entendue ou appelée. Les règles du Missouri imposent la signification régulière et, selon les procédures, un avis et une possibilité d’être entendu, mais ne formulent pas toutes une garantie générale identique.
correspondences.note_en: Article 14 prohibits judgment without a party having been heard or called. The Missouri provisions require proper service and, in particular proceedings, notice and an opportunity to be heard, but do not state one identical general guarantee.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 16 impose au juge de faire respecter la contradiction et interdit de fonder sa décision sur des éléments non discutés, notamment les moyens relevés d’office. Les règles du Missouri prévoient des échanges, audiences et possibilités de réponse dans certaines procédures, sans énoncer une obligation générale aussi large.
correspondences.note_en: Article 16 requires the court to preserve adversarial debate and bars reliance on undisputed submissions, including unraised legal grounds without an opportunity to comment. Missouri rules provide responses, hearings, and opportunities to address materials in specified proceedings, but not the same broad general duty.

Committee Note – 1974 This is the same as Rule 43(e) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 17 garantit à la partie qui n’a pas été informée d’une mesure ordonnée à son insu un recours approprié contre la décision qui lui fait grief. La Rule 92.02(b) autorise une ordonnance de référé sans préavis dans des conditions strictes et permet à la partie adverse, sur avis, d’en demander la dissolution ou la modification, mais seulement pour les temporary restraining orders.
correspondences.note_en: Article 17 guarantees an appropriate remedy to a party against whom a measure was ordered without prior knowledge. Rule 92.02(b) permits a temporary restraining order without notice under strict conditions and allows the adverse party, on notice, to move to dissolve or modify it, but it is limited to temporary restraining orders.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article définit l’ordonnance de référé comme une décision provisoire permettant au juge d’ordonner immédiatement les mesures nécessaires, sur demande contradictoire ou appelée. La Rule 92.02 organise les temporary restraining orders et preliminary injunctions, qui remplissent une fonction provisoire comparable, mais dans le cadre spécifique des injonctions.
correspondences.note_en: The article defines référé as a provisional decision allowing a judge to order immediately necessary measures upon an adversarial or summoned request. Rule 92.02 governs temporary restraining orders and preliminary injunctions, serving a comparable provisional function but within the specific injunction framework.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose un délai suffisant entre l’assignation et l’audience afin de permettre la préparation de la défense. La Rule 92.02 exige généralement un préavis raisonnable d’au moins vingt-quatre heures pour une temporary restraining order, tandis que la Rule 86.05 prévoit dix jours dans une procédure de condemnation.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires sufficient time between service and the hearing to allow preparation of the defense. Rule 92.02 generally requires reasonable notice of at least twenty-four hours for a temporary restraining order, while Rule 86.05 provides ten days in a condemnation proceeding.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article définit l’ordonnance sur requête comme une décision provisoire rendue sans débat contradictoire lorsque l’absence d’adversaire est justifiée. Les règles et textes du Missouri prévoient des mesures provisoires ex parte, mais seulement dans des domaines déterminés et sous des conditions spécifiques.
correspondences.note_en: The article defines an ex parte provisional decision available when the applicant is justified in not calling an opposing party. Missouri provides comparable ex parte provisional relief, but only in specified proceedings and subject to additional conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article impose une requête motivée, présentée en double, avec indication précise des pièces et, en cas d’instance, de la juridiction saisie; il prévoit aussi une présentation urgente au domicile du juge. Les textes du Missouri exigent surtout une requête vérifiée et l’exposé de faits précis ou d’un motif valable dans certaines procédures, sans reproduire les autres formalités françaises.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires a duplicate, reasoned application identifying supporting documents and, where applicable, the court seized, with an emergency filing option at the judge’s residence. Missouri provisions chiefly require a verified petition and specific facts or good cause in particular proceedings, without reproducing the other French formalities.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article exige la motivation, l’exécution au seul vu de la minute et la remise d’une copie de la requête et de l’ordonnance à la personne concernée. Le Missouri prévoit la motivation et l’entrée au dossier des mesures ex parte, ainsi que des règles de notification, sans reprendre exactement l’exécution sur minute.
correspondences.note_en: The article requires reasons, enforceability upon production of the original, and delivery of the application and order to the affected person. Missouri requires stated facts or reasons, filing and entry of ex parte orders, and notification mechanisms, but does not exactly replicate enforcement on the original.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 834 permet au président du tribunal judiciaire d’ordonner en urgence toute mesure non sérieusement contestable ou justifiée par un différend. La Rule 92.02 prévoit des mesures injonctives provisoires en cas de préjudice immédiat et irréparable, mais avec des conditions, une procédure et des effets différents; la Rule 92.01 désigne les juges compétents.
correspondences.note_en: Article 834 permits the president of the judicial court to order urgent relief where there is no serious dispute or where a dispute warrants it. Rule 92.02 provides provisional injunctive relief for immediate and irreparable harm, but under materially different conditions, procedures, and effects; Rule 92.01 identifies the authorized judges.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 835 autorise des mesures conservatoires ou de remise en état malgré une contestation sérieuse, pour prévenir un dommage imminent ou faire cesser un trouble manifestement illicite, ainsi qu’une provision lorsque l’obligation est incontestable. La Rule 92.02 offre une protection injonctive d’urgence, tandis que les deux sections RSMo visent spécifiquement la protection ou la garde d’enfants.
correspondences.note_en: Article 835 authorizes protective or restorative measures despite a serious dispute, to prevent imminent harm or end manifest unlawfulness, and permits payment on an obligation that is not seriously disputed. Rule 92.02 offers emergency injunctive protection, while the two RSMo sections are limited to child protection or custody.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 845 permet au juge, sur requête, d’ordonner des mesures urgentes sans débat contradictoire lorsque les circonstances l’exigent. La Rule 92.02(b) et le RSMo 455.513 prévoient également des mesures ex parte sur requête vérifiée, mais dans des cadres et sous des conditions spécifiques.
correspondences.note_en: Article 845 allows the judge, upon petition, to order urgent measures without adversarial proceedings when circumstances so require. Rule 92.02(b) and RSMo 455.513 likewise provide for ex parte relief on a verified petition, but within specific proceedings and subject to different conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 872 permet au président du tribunal de commerce, en urgence, d’ordonner toute mesure provisoire non sérieusement contestée ou justifiée par un différend. La Rule 92.02 encadre les injonctions et mesures de restraint d’urgence, mais selon des conditions, une procédure et des effets différents ; la Rule 92.01 concerne le pouvoir de les accorder.
correspondences.note_en: Article 872 authorizes the president of the commercial court to order urgent interim measures when they face no serious challenge or are justified by a dispute. Rule 92.02 governs emergency restraining and injunctive relief, but with different conditions, procedures, and effects; Rule 92.01 addresses judicial authority to grant injunctions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 873 vise les mesures conservatoires ou de remise en état en cas de dommage imminent ou de trouble manifestement illicite, ainsi que la provision lorsque l’obligation n’est pas sérieusement contestable. La Rule 92.02 couvre principalement les mesures injonctives d’urgence ; la Rule 68.02 permet la préservation de biens par un receiver, sans prévoir la provision française.
correspondences.note_en: Article 873 covers protective or restorative measures for imminent harm or manifestly unlawful interference, and provisional payment or performance when the obligation is not seriously disputed. Rule 92.02 chiefly addresses emergency injunctive relief; Rule 68.02 permits preservation of property through a receiver, but does not provide the French-style provisional award.

frcp.evidence: same as prior Rule 68.25. The sources of paragraph (C) are Rule 53 (a) of the Federal Rules of Civil Procedure

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 873-1 permet, à la demande d’une partie et en cas d’urgence, de renvoyer l’affaire de référé à une audience au fond, avec fixation de la date et garantie d’un délai suffisant pour la défense. La Rule 92.02(c)(3) autorise l’avancement et la jonction de l’examen au fond avec l’audience sur l’injonction préliminaire, mais selon une technique et des conditions différentes.
correspondences.note_en: Article 873-1 permits, on a party’s request and where urgent, referral from interim proceedings to a merits hearing with a fixed date and adequate defense time. Rule 92.02(c)(3) allows the merits trial to be advanced and consolidated with the preliminary-injunction hearing, but uses a different mechanism and conditions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet au président d’ordonner sur requête des mesures urgentes sans débat contradictoire lorsque les circonstances l’exigent. La Rule 92.02(b) prévoit une ordonnance restrictive temporaire sans préavis sous des conditions détaillées; l’article RSMo 455.513 prévoit une ordonnance ex parte de protection immédiate dans une matière spécialisée.
correspondences.note_en: The article authorizes urgent relief on petition without adversarial proceedings when circumstances require it. Rule 92.02(b) provides a no-notice temporary restraining order subject to detailed requirements, and RSMo 455.513 provides immediate ex parte protection orders in a specialized context; both are partial.

correspondences.note_fr: Le magistrat peut accorder une provision lorsque l'obligation n'est pas sérieusement contestable et ordonner toute mesure provisoire. La Rule 92.02 régit des mesures injonctives provisoires, tandis que RSMo 515.510 permet certaines mesures conservatoires par receiver, sans prévoir la provision française.
correspondences.note_en: The instructing judge may award interim payment where the obligation is not seriously disputed and order other provisional relief. Rule 92.02 governs temporary injunctive relief, while RSMo 515.510 permits certain preservation measures through a receiver, but neither provides the French summary-payment mechanism.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article permet à la personne visée de demander au juge ayant rendu l’ordonnance sa modification ou sa rétractation, par assignation, sans suspension des effets et après audition des intéressés. RSMo 455.060 prévoit la modification après motion et audience; Rule 92.02(b)(5) permet de demander la dissolution ou modification d’une ordonnance restrictive sans prévoir de suspension automatique. RSMo 455.040 complète le régime des audiences et notifications des ordonnances de protection.
correspondences.note_en: The article allows the respondent to seek modification or rescission from the issuing judge by summons, without suspending the order, after hearing the relevant persons. RSMo 455.060 provides modification after motion and hearing; Rule 92.02(b)(5) permits a motion to dissolve or modify a restraining order without an automatic stay. RSMo 455.040 adds protective-order hearing and service provisions.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article prévoit que les mesures urgentes entre époux sont ordonnées par le juge aux affaires familiales, en référé ou sur requête. Le § 452.200 prévoit une injonction contre le conjoint qui dilapide les biens, tandis que la Rule 92.02 encadre les injonctions provisoires, avec ou sans préavis; ces textes ne reproduisent toutefois ni la compétence du juge familial ni exactement les mesures de l’article 220-1.
correspondences.note_en: The article provides that urgent measures between spouses may be ordered by the family court judge on an interim or ex parte application. RSMo 452.200 authorizes an injunction against a spouse wasting property, while Rule 92.02 governs temporary injunctions with or without notice; neither reproduces the French family-court jurisdiction or the exact scope of article 220-1.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1468 permet au tribunal arbitral d’ordonner des mesures conservatoires ou provisoires, sauf les saisies et sûretés judiciaires réservées à l’État. La Rule 92.02 encadre fonctionnellement les injonctions et ordonnances temporaires, mais ne concerne ni l’arbitrage ni cette répartition de compétences.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1468 authorizes an arbitral tribunal to order interim or conservatory measures, while reserving seizures and judicial security measures to state courts. Rule 92.02 functionally addresses injunctions and temporary orders, but not arbitration or this allocation of jurisdiction.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 1537 confirme que la mise en œuvre d’une conciliation ou médiation conventionnelle n’empêche pas le juge d’ordonner une mesure d’instruction, provisoire ou conservatoire. Les règles du Missouri régissent certaines de ces mesures, mais ne prévoient pas expressément leur maintien ou leur ordonnance malgré une procédure amiable conventionnelle.
correspondences.note_en: Article 1537 provides that conventional conciliation or mediation does not prevent the court from ordering an investigative, provisional, or conservatory measure. The Missouri rules govern particular forms of such measures, but do not expressly address ordering them notwithstanding conventional ADR.

norms.heading: Injunction Pending Appeal

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
When an appeal is taken from a judgment granting, dissolving, or denying an injunction, the court in its discretion may suspend, modify, restore, or grant an injunction during the pendency of the appeal upon such terms as to bond or otherwise as it considers proper for the security of the rights of the adverse party.

#### Committee Note – 1981

The source is the first sentence of Fed. R. Civ. P. 62(c).

source_ids.text_source: Perplexity search-index copy of the courts.mo.gov page (pplx_sdk.content.snippets)

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 517-4 impose au premier président de statuer en référé sur les demandes relatives à l’exécution provisoire et exclut le pourvoi. La Rule 81.10 traite de la demande de caution et du sursis pendant l’appel, tandis que les Rules 92.04 et 92.03 permettent à la juridiction d’appel de maintenir ou modifier certaines mesures pendant l’appel, sans reprendre les mêmes règles de procédure ni d’exclusion du pourvoi.
correspondences.note_en: Article 517-4 requires the first president to rule in summary proceedings on matters concerning provisional enforcement and makes the decision non-reviewable by cassation. Rule 81.10 concerns a bond and a stay during appeal, while Rules 92.04 and 92.03 authorize appellate preservation or modification of measures during appeal, but do not reproduce the same procedure or bar on further review.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article 956 permet au premier président, en urgence et pendant l’appel, d’ordonner en référé toute mesure non sérieusement contestable ou justifiée par un différend. Les Rules 92.03 et 92.04 reconnaissent des pouvoirs comparables de l’instance d’appel pendant l’appel, mais principalement pour les injonctions et la préservation du statu quo ou de l’efficacité du jugement.
correspondences.note_en: Article 956 permits the first president, in urgent appellate proceedings, to order interim measures facing no serious dispute or justified by a dispute. Rules 92.03 and 92.04 provide comparable appellate powers during an appeal, but chiefly for injunctions and preserving the status quo or the effectiveness of the judgment.

correspondences.note_fr: Le premier président peut ordonner, sur requête et sans débat contradictoire, des mesures urgentes de sauvegarde pendant l'appel. La Rule 92.04 reconnaît un pouvoir général de la juridiction d'appel ou de son juge pour préserver le statu quo ou l'efficacité du jugement, tandis que la Rule 92.03 vise plus étroitement les injonctions pendant l'appel.
correspondences.note_en: The first president may order urgent protective measures ex parte during an appeal. Rule 92.04 recognizes a broad appellate power to preserve the status quo or the effectiveness of a later judgment, while Rule 92.03 more narrowly concerns injunctions pending appeal.

norms.heading: Petition in Mandamus – Contents – Exhibits

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
Application for a writ of mandamus shall be made by filing a petition in mandamus in the appropriate court.

The petition in mandamus shall contain a statement of the facts, the relief sought, and a statement of the reasons why the writ should issue.

The petition in mandamus shall be accompanied by suggestions in support thereof.
A copy of any order, opinion, record or part thereof, document, or other item that may be essential to an understanding of the matters set forth in the petition in mandamus shall be attached as exhibits if not set forth therein. The pages of the exhibits shall be numbered consecutively.

An index of all exhibits also shall be attached. Exhibits shall be identified in the index by number or letter and page and, in addition, shall be described so that the court can distinguish the exhibits.

#### Committee Note – 1981

This is new.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article soumet les demandes relatives au prénom à la procédure écrite ordinaire et limite l’exécution provisoire aux cas où le juge l’ordonne. La Rule 95.01 encadre la pétition de changement de nom, tandis que les RSMo 506.110 et 509.010 traitent respectivement de l’introduction par pétition et des actes de procédure; aucun ne reprend expressément la règle d’exécution provisoire.
correspondences.note_en: The article subjects given-name applications to ordinary written procedure and makes provisional enforcement available only when ordered. Rule 95.01 governs the contents of a name-change petition, while RSMo 506.110 and 509.010 address commencement by petition and pleadings; none expressly reproduces the provisional-enforcement rule.

correspondences.note_fr: La demande est introduite par requête remise ou adressée au greffe; elle peut aussi porter sur les prénoms et l’avocat n’est pas obligatoire. Rule 53.01 prévoit le dépôt d’une petition pour commencer une action, et Rule 95.01 encadre une petition de changement de nom, mais aucun ne couvre entièrement cette demande spéciale.
correspondences.note_en: The application is initiated by a petition filed with or sent to the clerk; it may also seek a name change, and counsel is not mandatory. Rule 53.01 provides for commencing an action by petition, and Rule 95.01 governs name-change petitions, but neither fully covers this special application.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article organise le consentement de l’enfant majeur au changement de nom consécutif à une modification de filiation et sa réception par certaines autorités. Les Rules 95.01 et 95.04 encadrent la demande et l’ordonnance de changement de nom, sans prévoir ce consentement ni ses formes particulières.
correspondences.note_en: The article governs an adult child’s consent to a name change following a change in filiation and specifies who may receive it. Rules 95.01 and 95.04 regulate name-change petitions and orders, but do not provide this consent mechanism or its specified formalities.

norms.heading: Joint Petition for Family

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
Parents and minor children may join in a petition for change of name and the petition shall state the facts herein required of the parents and the name of the minor children may be changed at the discretion of the court.

#### Committee Note – 1981

This is new.

It is designed to allow one petition to take the place of several where an entire family is seeking a change of name.

norms.heading: Petition for Change of a Minor's Name – Notice to or Consent of Parents

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
When a minor files a petition for change of name the written consent of each known parent shall be filed. If the written consent of each known parent is not filed, a copy of the petition together with a notice stating the date of the hearing shall be served on each known parent not consenting not less than thirty days before the date of the hearing. The service shall be by registered or certified mail addressed to the last known address of the nonconsenting parent. Service shall be proved by the certificate of the clerk that he has mailed a copy of the petition and notice by registered or certified mail.

#### Committee Note – 1981

This is new.

norms.heading: Publication of Notice of Change of Name

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure

norms.text:
When a change of name is granted notice of the change shall be published at least once each week for three consecutive weeks in a newspaper of general circulation published in the county where the change of name was granted. If there is no such newspaper, then the publication shall be in a newspaper designated by the court. Proof of the publication shall be filed with the clerk within ten days after the date of last publication.

#### Committee Note – 1981

The source is prior Rule 95.03.

The last sentence requiring proof of publication to be filed is new and it was added so that the record would show that the publication was made.

norms.heading: Right to Partition in General

path.label: Supreme Court Rules — Rules of Civil Procedure
Rule 96 — Partition of Real and Personal Property

norms.text:
Owners of interests in land in joint tenancy or tenancy in common, including estates in fee, for life, or for years, may bring an action for partition, if the same can be done without great prejudice to the parties in interest, and, if not, then for a sale of the property, and a division of the proceeds thereof.

#### Committee Note – 1981

This is substantially the same as prior Rule 96.01.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article rend applicables les règles procédurales du partage et attribue au juge familial les procédures d’apposition de scellés et d’état descriptif. Les Rules 96.01, 96.08 et 96.32 organisent le partage de biens réels ou personnels; le RSMo 452.330 règle la division des biens matrimoniaux, mais aucun texte ne prévoit les scellés et l’état descriptif.
correspondences.note_en: The article applies partition procedures and assigns the family judge authority over sealing and inventory proceedings. Rules 96.01, 96.08, and 96.32 govern partition of real or personal property, while RSMo 452.330 governs marital-property division; none addresses sealing and inventory specifically.

correspondences.note_fr: L’article désigne le président du tribunal judiciaire et impose une procédure particulière pour certaines demandes successorales, notamment dans un partage amiable. Les règles 96.01 et 96.32 organisent la partition de biens immobiliers ou mobiliers, tandis que la règle 41.01 encadre l’application des règles civiles en matière successorale; aucune ne reproduit la compétence ni la procédure française.
correspondences.note_en: The article assigns specified succession applications to the president of the judicial court and prescribes a particular procedure, including for amicable partition. Rules 96.01 and 96.32 govern partition of real or personal property, while Rule 41.01 addresses civil-rule applicability in probate proceedings; none reproduces the French jurisdiction or procedure.
